German singer-songwriter Alice Merton claimed she had expressly denied the rapper's clearance request due to his history of antisemitism.

Ye (formerly Kanye West) has settled a lawsuit that accused him of sampling a song by German singer-songwriter Alice Merton even though she had rejected clearance due to the rapper’s history of antisemitism.

Sebagaimana diketahui, a nov. 6 court filing, obtained by Billboard, stated that Ye and Merton have reached a settlement “conditioned on the parties’ completion of certain performance obligations. ” Deal terms were not disclosed, and reps for both sides did not immediately return requests for comment.

Berdasarkan laporan, merton sued ye last year, alleging his 2024 track “gun to my head” sampled her earlier song “blindside” without permission. Merton said she had expressly denied Ye’s clearance request months earlier because, as a direct descendant of Holocaust survivors, she did not want to be associated with the rapper’s past antisemitic remarks.

Sebagaimana diketahui, ye’s lawyers argued in response that merton did not have the proper evidence for a copyright claim. They also pointed out that “Gun to My Head” has never been available on streaming; it was released on a digital deluxe version of Vultures 2, which was only available for purchase during a two-day period in 2024.

Berdasarkan laporan, merton’s case had been scheduled to go to trial this coming march. In October — a month before the settlement was reached — a judge denied Ye’s request to remove all references to the Holocaust and antisemitism from the lawsuit.

Sebagaimana diketahui, ye has been sued more than a dozen times over the course of his career for allegedly using unlicensed samples and interpolations in his music. The rapper has settled many of these claims. He took one to trial for the first time earlier this year, and a jury ultimately held him liable for infringing an instrumental track on an early version of his chart-topping 2021 album Donda.

Sebagaimana diketahui, meanwhile, ye’s career has been mired in controversy around his antisemitism since 2022. He issued a lengthy apology in the Wall Street Journal this past January for years of public hate speech, including praise of Hitler and selling swastika T-shirts. Ye wrote in this apology, which preceded the release of his latest album Bully, that these controversial comments had stemmed from a 2002 car crash that caused severe brain damage and bipolar disorder.

Berdasarkan laporan, “i regret and am deeply mortified by my actions in that state, and am committed to accountability, treatment and meaningful change,” ye wrote. I am not a Nazi or an antisemite. I love Jewish people. “It does not excuse what I did, though. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, ye has since worked to mount a comeback, playing to huge crowds at an ongoing run of stadium shows this year. Senator Rick Scott (R-Fla. But the rapper’s past is still haunting him, and shows in the U. ) also ran a public, though unsuccessful, campaign to stop Ye from performing at Tampa, Fla. K. and Poland have been canceled due to government concerns about his previous antisemitic statements. ’s Raymond James Stadium in June.

Sebagaimana diketahui, griffith also worked on the soundtracks for films including pretty woman and the bodyguard, the latter of which launched “i will always love you. ” After Arista, he lead A&R at Manhattan Records, where, most notably, he worked with Richard Marx.

Diungkapkan bahwa “gerry never got the accolades he so deserved for discovering whitney houston, but we knew the real deal,” brenda andrews, a former senior vp of rondor music international, said in a statement. May he rest peacefully with all of our brothers and sisters that have made their place in Heaven. ” He knew HIT SONGS! All of us will miss him. “He gave me two hits out of the box with her, “I Wanna Dance With Somebody” and “How Will I Know. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, as music manager and publisher deirdre o’hara wrote: “early in my music publishing career, i was very fortunate to connect with gerry griffith. One of my proudest moments was urging Gerry to see Whitney Houston … and the rest is history. ”.

Griffith is survived by his two daughters and two sons.

#324. Russell Brand Was Sentenced for Rape and Sexual Assault on Monday. By Friday, Netflix Had a Sleazy Doc Ready to Go

📅 13 Nov 2026

Russell Brand Was Sentenced for Rape and Sexual Assault on Monday. By Friday, Netflix Had a Sleazy Doc Ready to Go

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.indiewire.com/features/commentary/netflix-russell-brand-documentary-insights-1235227726/

Berdasarkan laporan, the term that comes to mind most is “ambulance-chasing. ” Earlier this week, just one week after Russell Brand was convicted of rape and sexual assault and two days after he was sentenced to 10 years and six months in prison for his crimes, word spread that Netflix was prepping a documentary on the comedian-turned-criminal.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, olivia isaacs’ documentary has been in the works for a while. Deadline’s initial story on the project even noted that it “was referenced during the trial” and that while “giving evidence at London’s Southwark Crown Court, Mark Pinheiro, a former friend of Brand, said he had been approached by a producer about the Netflix show. ” Related Stories David O. Russell’s ‘Madden’ Biopic Is Out Next Week — Does Anybody Know or Care? In Shana Feste’s Films, Gender-Flipping Cinema’s ‘Tradition of Celebrating Damaged Men’ Is Its Own Reward.

Berdasarkan laporan, but that the project — “russell brand: open secret,” a slim and unfocused documentary feature that clocks in at just under 90 minutes — was being dropped on the streamer to ride the wave of interest after brand’s conviction and sentencing felt distasteful. How essential, after all, could this be? And what could it tell us about Brand’s actual trial, sentencing, and conviction?.

Diungkapkan bahwa turns out, not much. Isaacs’ film doesn’t get into the trial until its final five minutes (counting its end credits to boot), when it uses title cards to share the conviction news, note that all of the allegations contained in the film itself “pre-date” those that led to the conviction, and make clear that Brand’s legal team was contacted after the Monday conviction and chose not to respond. That’s perhaps the most interesting part of the film’s literally tacked-on final moments: a desire to show its work when it comes to the journalism and attendant standards behind Brand’s long-simmering takedown.

Sebagaimana diketahui, other elements are far less successful, as isaacs’ film leans hard on tired tropes and cloying conventions. Captions frequently mention “[unsettling music playing]” or “[dramatic music playing]” during the most benign moments. Old footage of Brand, from home video to early stand-up gigs, is played slowly, all the better to maximize the sense that something is wrong with this man. Far more effective are interviews with those who were allegedly victimized by Brand, but those are often drowned out by played-out techniques.

The film opens with a typical “rise and fall” style montage, charting Brand’s humble beginnings, meteoric rise to fame, profound injection into the cultural consciousness (he met the queen! and also Tom Cruise!), stumble into right-wing ideology, and eventual criminal convictions for horrific acts the film posits everyone knew about forever.

Berdasarkan laporan, it is, after all, called “russell brand: open secret. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, isaacs’ film lacks a thesis beyond the general idea that everyone knew brand was a creep from the jump. She assembles a hodgepodge of talking heads to hammer that home, including fellow comedians, some genuinely freaked out ex-girlfriends, a handful of accusers (including one who, reticent to appear on camera, is replaced with an actress, one of the film’s most thoughtful choices), and some bizarrely starry-eyed commentators (journalist George Monbiot comes across particularly badly here, zipping from talking about his early delight in Brand and his now-held belief that Brand’s far-right switch is the most horrifying aspect of all of this, oof).

Berdasarkan laporan, most compelling are times journalists rosamund urwin and charlotte wace, who worked tirelessly to investigate myriad accusations against brand for years (urwin first began to look into brand in january of 2019). Even smushed up against a herky-jerky timeline and a loose sense of purpose, the way that Urwin and Wace talk about the precise nature of their work, what they can and cannot report, the women they spoke to, and the ways in which they were nearly shut down (and, in fact, many other investigations of its ilk were allegedly turned off) is both gripping and necessary.

With more time and better access, the film could have focused more on the police and legal minds that helped build the case against Brand, but in the rush to get this out in the world, that was surely not a major aim.

Sebagaimana diketahui, by its midpoint, isaacs’ film turns its lens on the culture that helped give rise to brand, the wild “noughties” when “ladette culture” ruled and being overtly sexy and crude was de rigueur. Women were into Brand! Being ruthlessly unfunny and breathlessly boorish was hot! Also, his dad was mean to him! Diddy and David Walliams jump scares! These are some of the insights on offer in “Open Secret,” and the only thing truly revealing about them is how huge of a mistake it was to let someone as outwardly disgusting and deeply unwitty as Brand get into a place where he could pick and choose his “damsels” or his “whores,” depending on who is talking about them.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the film speed-runs through the last few years of brand’s life and career, as he pivots into far-right shock politics and christianity just as the walls are starting to close in on him. Brand may have alleged that his former cadre of famous friends and stalwarts won’t “touch him with a barge pole” these days, but the film’s distinct lack of bigger talking heads stands out. That could stand some further interrogation, too, but there’s simply no time for that. (Well, there is, but not if you want to be a part of this news cycle. ).

Sebagaimana diketahui, the four-day gap between brand’s conviction and the film’s release is zippy, even for netflix, which has gotten progressively speedier with its true crime joints. In July of 2024, it was announced that Netflix would release a multi-part Karen Read documentary, just days after her first murder trial ended in a mistrial due to a hung jury on July 1, 2024. Three episodes dropped earlier this month.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in january of 2026, the streamer announced a lucy letby project with “unprecedented access” after the crown prosecution service (cps) announced it would bring no further criminal charges against the former nurse, who was sentenced to life imprisonment for a slew of charges of murder and attempted murder of infants in her care following a review of additional allegations. “The Truth and Tragedy of Moriah Wilson” was first publicly announced in February of 2026, almost three years after Kaitlin Armstrong was convicted of first-degree murder of the cyclist in November of 2023.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “russell brand: open secret” will surely capture lots of eyeballs as this part of the news cycle winds down, but what the film trades for immediacy, it more than loses in actual insight. Part two can’t be far behind. Let’s just hope it takes far more time to make and far more consideration to craft.

“Russell Brand: Open Secret” is now streaming on Netflix.

Surely Brooker and writer-star Diane Morgan know that Cunk and her gimmick won’t play forever, so Cunk on Cinema may mean they’ve decided to take the premise about as far as it can go without becoming a parody of a thing that’s already a parody.

But the ratio of punchlines that fizzle to punchlines that hit is probably closer to even than at any previous point in the franchise.

Still, Cunk on Cinema offers more laughs than just about anything else you’re likely to watch this month, and I’m prepared to follow the miseducation of Philomena Cunk until the wheels entirely come off.

Cunk on Cinema is structurally simple, as television presenter Cunk (Morgan) takes viewers on a history of filmic media going all the way back to, well, the absence of movies.

Diungkapkan bahwa “movies haven’t always been with us. In fact, for centuries Earth was a barren wasteland devoid of entertainment content,” she observes, walking through a sea of classic paintings and noting, “For centuries, eyes were literally useless, because there was nothing worth looking at. ”.

She traces the advent of photography and then moving pictures, touching on landmarks like The Arrival of a Train at La Ciotat (“It’s almost as boring as Ben Affleck,” she notes), The Birth of a Nation (“A typically woke Hollywood fantasy”), and into the comedies of Charlie Chaplin (“To this day, the only homeless person it’s okay to openly laugh at”) and Buster Keaton.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, i don’t want to accuse cunk on cinema of being intellectually nourishing by any stretch of the imagination, but as bite-sized introductions to film studies go, it has some validity. Working her way through her usual assortment of photogenic backdrops, from film studios to the base of the Hollywood sign to various libraries and repositories, Cunk touches at least briefly on a range of noteworthy, properly contextualized bits of history — from an acceptable definition of the Kuleshov effect to a rudimentary explanation of the Hays Code to an acknowledgement of the impact of TV on the films of the 1950s and 1960s.

Berdasarkan laporan, cunk’s droll approach to classic films and the medium’s evolution alternates between willfully ignorant and perceptively counter-logical, going amusingly deep on e. as a grooming narrative and resorting to social media-friendly one-liners like, “Do you have to have seen the first 2000 films in the series in order to understand 2001?” It’s possible that some parts of Cunk on Cinema benefit from knowing about the films and industry conventions she’s lampooning. T. But I’m not sure how knowledgable one need be to find it funny to keep referring to Eisenstein’s Battleship Potemkin as “Batshit Pumpkin” over and over. I found it funny over and over.

As always, Cunk can’t do it alone and she’s assembled a group of experts, from the usual dry British intellectuals to a scattering of film critics to an amusing range of cinematic craftsmen (mostly men) to actual A-listers including Michael Bay and Benedict Cumberbatch.

A key piece of the appeal of Cunk has been tracing how realistic it is for her subjects not to know what she’s doing as she peppers them with questions like “What was The Jizz Slinger?” or, regarding the behavior of Taxi Driver antihero Travis Bickle, remarks that “If they remade it today, he’d be violating Uber’s code of conduct, wouldn’t he?”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, i’m guessing the screening process for cunk on cinema had to be different from her earlier series and that more people probably had to be rejected for being excessively in on the joke. Moreover, it’s easy to notice that Cunk has needed to shift her style of inquiry in a way that’s interesting, but increasingly repetitive.

Sebagaimana diketahui, if your interview subject is in on the joke, the worst thing you can do is ask a lengthy, ridiculous question based on an absurd premise — the meat and potatoes of her finest moments, previously — because if they laugh or, perish the thought, attempt to counter with a joke of their own, you’ve wasted a lot of rope just to hang yourself. But if you ask a simple question based on a malapropism or misheard or misread title or concept, at the very least you’ll get several seconds of well-earned confusion, and then several more seconds of confusion while the interviewee tries to come up with a sincere response or a joke. That confusion is gold, or as much gold as you happen to find in jokes like “The Jizz Slinger. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, with most of the scholars and scribes, cunk on cinema settles for “confusion,” as opposed to the delicious obtuseness that earlier seasons yielded. It’s good for chuckles, but it denies viewers those moments of brilliance from previous series, when Philomena Cunk would actually intrigue an expert with a bizarre supposition or only half-jesting theory.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, it’s fairly reasonable to believe that a serious-minded historian or zoologist might not know philomena cunk and her thing, but it’s harder to imagine an entertainment journalist or film critic with no awareness of this increasingly long-running franchise. But not impossible!.

Some of these interview subjects are performers, or at least people with years of experience talking to the press or appearing in the public eye, which forces viewers to engage in guesswork.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, so … benedict cumberbatch? pretty clearly in on the joke and intentionally giving cunk only stone-faced bafflement. Die Hard scribe Steven E. de Souza? Pretty clearly not in on the joke and being genuine in not understanding what he’s in the middle of.

Berdasarkan laporan, and michael bay? this could be one of the year’s great debates, like a tv equivalent of you can see everything. At the same time, Michael Bay has an ego, and it’s possible he went in with one goal — not looking like a total fool — and that goal went out the window, or very nearly went out the window, in the face of one rambling trademark Cunk family story. Michael Bay has a team. They must have briefed him and advised him on how to react to certain pieces of obvious bait. This puts Bay in a liminal space halfway between professional and cool (as his team must’ve wanted him to appear) and thoroughly risible (as schadenfreude-hungry audiences may crave).

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, (disclaimer: my guesses could all be off! cumberbatch might have been sincerely perplexed, de souza might have been playing cunk like a fiddle, and michael bay? well, i should know better than to think i know what’s in michael bay’s mind. ).

Sebagaimana diketahui, morgan remains a droll genius, never better than in the walk-and-talk monologue on a studio lot in the final episode. D. The material is so perfectly tailored to her voice that she can get laughs even on flaccid punchlines that sound like outtakes from Brooker’s angry political comedy (see his Wipe shows) rather than from Cunk, who does not feel like the sort of character who would bother with a J. Vance joke out of nowhere. Now Cunk’s obsession with AI and Brooker’s contempt for it? Those mesh admirably.

Sebagaimana diketahui, simply put, the cunk formula still works, but it probably can’t work forever. I’m available for talking head segments and I promise to look confused when she mispronounces “Quibi. Now bring on Cunk on TV. ”.

The nearly two-and-a-half-hour KISS: End of the Road film shows in intimate detail that the conclusion of that phase of the band’s career was emotional, triumphant and trying.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, directed by dj viola, who also helmed the 2021 a&e documentary kisstory, the chronicle focuses on the final 2023 leg of the pandemic-interrupted end of the road world tour, which started in south america and played north america, europe and australia before wrapping up with homecoming performances dec. 1-2 at Madison Square Garden in New York City.

Diungkapkan bahwa noting that kisstory was “what we call a ‘womb-to-tomb’ documentary,” viola tells billboard, “i wanted end of the road to be almost the antithesis of that approach. Rather than having the guys tell us what happened, I wanted audiences to experience it as it was happening, from the first of their final 50 shows all the way to Madison Square Garden. ” He and his crew became embedded flies on the wall during the trek, capturing planning meetings, backstage intrigue and plenty of onstage highlights, as well as interviews with band members, manager Doc McGhee, Simmons’ and Stanley’s wives and others.

Berdasarkan laporan, “for 50 years,” viola notes, “kiss has been protective of what happens behind the curtain. After 50 years, that dedication hasn’t diminished one bit. This time, the band opened that curtain completely. What you discover is that beneath all the makeup, pyro and spectacle is an unwavering commitment to giving their fans the greatest show possible. Everyone says they want to show the ‘warts and all,’ but very few actually mean it. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, there are warts aplenty, too, including: production difficulties early on that created significant tension in the touring party; simmons being briefly incapacitated by dehydration during a concert in brazil; and stanley suffering from a severe flu that led to the cancellation of nine shows and put the last stretch of the tour in jeopardy. There are touching scenes as well, with the band and those around them talking about reaching the end of touring life. Stanley and Simmons both choke up during the final concert while talking from the stage about their parents and growing up in New York, and Simmons even shoos the camera crew away as he and Stanley exchange sentiments during that night’s sound check.

The film ends with the two men meeting, post-tour, for a convivial conversation at a deli in Bel Air, Calif.

Berdasarkan laporan, “the trick to being unobtrusive in documentary filmmaking is to be ubiquitous,” viola says. “You have to be there for the dullest moments as well as the most exciting ones…. It’s a strange balance, but that’s where the best moments come from. Eventually, you’re just another person in the room. You have to become part of the team while remaining as invisible as possible. The more you’re around, the more people stop thinking about the camera. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, he adds that, “the trust we’d established during kisstory was essential. I was there to authentically capture what was happening, good or bad. They knew I wasn’t there to manufacture controversy. KISS allowed me into virtually every corner of their world, from rehearsals and travel to putting on their makeup, standing onstage during the shows and being there afterward when the makeup came off and they dissected the night’s performance. ”.

Stanley says the band was not bothered by the constant camera presence, explaining that at this point, he and Simmons are more comfortable letting fans inside aspects of KISS that were previously kept under wraps — and deliberately so.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “it’s more appropriate to do now,” he says. It’s all very encompassing, and always has been…. At this point, it’s interesting to let people go behind it and in some ways, it makes it bigger because it’s such a Herculean effort to do what we’ve done. “It’s famously remembered that for the early years of the band, nobody ever saw us without makeup and that was part of the mystique, part of building this larger-than-life persona. To have a band go on stage 50 years later and people go, ‘They look the same as they did,’ well, that doesn’t happen by chance. I think people can appreciate that now and realize that there’s a real person behind Superman with a Marshall amp. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the end of the road film nods to the past with historical footage, and it also provides a glimpse into the future by showing the group working with sweden’s pophouse entertainment — which acquired kiss’ catalog and trademarks for a reported $300 million during 2024 — on the digital avatar show, which was previewed at the final madison square garden date. They’re very cognizant of the fact that the same-old isn’t the way to do it… and want to make it easier for fans who want to control the content. “They’re infusing so much money into KISS; you’re gonna have theme parks and cartoons and movies…just some amazing stuff coming. “They’re great new partners,” Simmons says. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the kiss avatar show is still a work in progress, but simmons predicts that it will arrive “in the next year to two years, at a place that is soon to be announced. ” Stanley notes that “it’s far more complicated than I certainly anticipated. They’re really putting a lot of effort  into it. But the rewards are that much greater, too. It’s quite complex. ” And he clarifies that it will likely be something different from what’s expected.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “the idea was never to replicate a concert. That’s what we’re creating. And the idea was never to do something that was appealing exclusively to a KISS fan; we wanted to create a must-see, so to speak, regardless of your taste in music. “It’s to create an experience and almost make us your tour guides into something unworldly, and yet totally based in the music. That’s not what this is about,” Stanley says. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the kiss biopic is also moving forward, with joseph mcginty “mcg” nichol directing and casting. It’s very slow going; you can rush something out but, frankly, I love being in a position where if we can’t do a film that I’m proud of, I don’t need to do a film. “It’s still in motion, and that’s all I can say. It just doesn’t matter that much. “Anybody who’s ever been involved in film knows you can get old waiting for a film to get made,” Stanley says. It would be a nice feather in the cap, but it better be a good-looking feather or I don’t want it. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, simmons and stanley may have more to reveal at the kiss kruise. Both have been preparing for the band’s performances as well as the Frehley tribute, an all-star event during which Frehley’s band will back a roster of guests, including alumnus guitarist Bruce Kulick.

Diungkapkan bahwa the rock and roll over sets, meanwhile, feature a new mix by original album producer eddie kramer, along with outtakes, alternative mixes, demos and a live 1977 performance from japan. “And I’m certainly open to looking into other people working on other albums and go in and reimagine them, rebirth them. “To have Eddie Kramer go in and rethink things was great,” Stanley says. I’m always in favor of making something better when it’s possible. ”.

None of that has affected the way Simmons and Stanley view their honor, however.

What you think politically, that’s for the ballot box. President Trump is our president, and that’s it. ”.

#343. In Shana Feste’s Films, Gender-Flipping Cinema’s ‘Tradition of Celebrating Damaged Men’ Is Its Own Reward

📅 13 Nov 2026

In Shana Feste’s Films, Gender-Flipping Cinema’s ‘Tradition of Celebrating Damaged Men’ Is Its Own Reward

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.indiewire.com/features/interviews/heartland-shana-feste-jessica-chastain-netflix-movie-1235227350/

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, shana feste knows her filmography might be a bit tough to pin down. Some directors like to stick to a certain genre. Not Feste. Others enter a franchise and never look back. Not Feste. Some only like to work with certain stars. Not Feste.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, but over the course of nearly two decades behind the camera, feste has carved out a particular sweet spot, regardless of the genre or the cast or the wider world her stories fit inside: she likes complicated women. Not unlikable women, but messy women, contradictory women, women who get things done their own way. It’s a signature unto itself.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “my filmmaking, my history, people have not really known what to do with me. “But I do find that they’re all starting to build into each other, especially the trajectory from ‘Country Strong’ to ‘Run Sweetheart Run’ to ‘Heartland. ’ I’ve always been drawn to women who don’t behave correctly. I’ve always been interested in women who don’t grieve correctly, who mother incorrectly, who love incorrectly. I just want women to have the freedom to behave in this contradictory, destructive, funny, selfish way and be given the same freedom that male characters are given. I’m making a comedy, I’m making a horror film, I’m making a genre thriller,” Feste told IndieWire during a recent interview. ” Related Stories Jensen Huang’s Biopic Feels Inevitable — The Right One Might Be Impossible Miles Teller Opens Up About ‘Paper Tiger,’ Adam Driver, and Losing His Home Before Filming James Gray’s Movie.

Sebagaimana diketahui, another shared characteristic between feste’s complicated women: they may be messy or unexpected, but they tend to get shit done. She’s thrust back into that world after her niece, rising star Charlie Heart (Carter Faith), goes missing. In her new film “Heartland,” getting shit done is at the center of the story, as the Nashville-set drama follows Jessica Chastain as Misty Jones, a former country-singing superstar who left the business after her designation as the, ahem, “cunt of country” became too much to bear. Misty, being Misty, takes it upon herself to get to the bottom of an increasingly dark and twisted mystery, no matter what it takes.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “i am a mom of three, 51, and i’m like, ‘let’s write about some women who get shit done,’” she said. But when women behave similarly, they could be labeled as hysterical or dramatic or that word, unlikable. I’m living in the South now that I see those women every day and am inspired by them. I want to prove that wrong. “I find a lot of those women exist. We have this long-established cinematic tradition of celebrating damaged men. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, for the (complicated, messy, extremely capable) character of misty, feste said, she initially tapped into her longtime love of film noir. She always gravitated toward the Humphrey Bogart types, she said, but wondered what might happen if they gave those sorts of roles to women. That also fed into the dark underbelly of the Nashville scene that the film interrogates, a perfectly noir-ish idea.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “it could have been any city, but specifically this dark underbelly had to do with the music world,” feste said. He had just been arrested, and things were coming into light. We thought, oh wow, this is such a topical moment. When we were making the movie, a lot of conversation around Diddy was happening. It was an experience that I’ve experienced in our industry, and it was all too relevant. And I’m like, it’s always topical, sadly. Whether we’re Epstein, Diddy, Weinstein, this is always going to be in the world, sadly. “Sadly, it was a common experience for a lot of artists that I spoke with. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, but feste is also someone who loves this world and wants to celebrate what’s good and true about it. “Country Strong” was about making it — and maybe even making it again — even at great personal cost. “Heartland” just ratchets that sensibility up.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “i wanted to lean into the secrets and the dark corners and the underbelly, but i also will always celebrate the artistry and the storytelling of country music,” she said. So to point out someone who doesn’t deserve country music, I mean, that’s a big insult for me. ’ It takes a lot to deserve country music in my eyes. Country music is like the apex of storytelling. “Misty says one line that really speaks so much to me about what the film is: ‘You don’t deserve country music. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, feste started writing “heartland” around four years ago, mostly because she was really missing the world of country music that framed her 2010 music drama “country strong. ” “My father died about eight years ago, and I found myself listening to a lot of country music when he died,” she said. And I realized, oh, I’m really missing my father. “In the years after he died, going back to the music that he loved, that he used to play for me in the car when we were driving on road trips, I realized that when you’re a writer, you don’t know quite why you write something until years later. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, she was also eager to reteam with her “country strong” collaborators jenno topping and randall poster, two people who feste said have believed in her the most over the course of her career. “So having them help me tell this story was just monumental. (Topping and Poster both produced “Heartland,” with Poster also serving as music supervisor, as he did on “Country Strong. It was being with someone that you knew had your back the entire time. ”) “When I’m having my darkest days about, I don’t know, me and what I create and my career, knowing that they believe in me has always been such a huge lift,” Feste said. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, if “heartland” sees misty feeling ill at ease in the very spaces that used to celebrate her talent, feste had the opposite experience. Six films into her directing career, she said “Heartland” let her approach her work in an entirely new way. And it felt good.

Diungkapkan bahwa “what was really valuable with this experience is that i felt completely comfortable saying, ‘i don’t know,’ and i don’t know if i’ve ever felt that way,” she said. It was only working with this group of filmmakers, Jenno and Randy and [production designer] Naomi [Shohan], some of my heads of production, that I knew that they saw my vulnerability not as a weakness, but as a strength. I was able to say, ‘I don’t know, what do you think?’ That’s where a very new form of collaboration happened that I haven’t experienced in my career, and with Jessica as well. “Certainly not with my first few films, feeling like as a woman, I had to know every answer from every head of department immediately. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, casting chastain was an easy call for feste. She wanted someone who could sing and who was admired in this space, but Chastain’s way of working and approach to on-set life gave Feste more to work with than she could have dreamed.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “i always want my films, especially when we’re shooting a movie that takes place in nashville, to feel authentic, and i knew jessica already had a huge buy-in from this audience. “And Jessica can sing, and that is another qualifier. But I think most of all, Jessica is one of the biggest champions of other women that I’ve ever met. The South, they love her from ‘George & Tammy,’” Feste said. Whenever I’m making any kind of movie with music, I want the actors to be able to sing their own material. ”.

It was freeing for Feste to say “I don’t know,” but Chastain also made it clear that she was there to support Feste’s vision and leadership.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “there were certain times on set where it would get a little loud or kind of disorderly, and people would be talking and having opinions, and no matter what, she’d be like, ‘shana, sorry, i couldn’t hear you,’ and it was like this just gentle reminder, ‘this is who is leading the ship right now for me,’” the filmmaker recalled. “It was done in the classiest, most polite way. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, that approach turned the collaboration into more of a partnership. When Chastain had an idea, Feste was eager to listen. Even a decade ago, she said, that might not have been so easy for her.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “if i had been the director that i was 10 years ago, it would’ve scared me to death, because jessica is not afraid to come into a scene and say, ‘ok, wait, that might not be serving us. This wasn’t a scary experience. And to be able to relinquish control and admit when my idea wasn’t the best idea and she’s coming in with a stronger idea because she is Jessica Chastain? She has done the work. Let’s throw that idea out of the window. It was actually going to elevate the scene and make it work even better. She has made this character so rich. “As a director, I’m planning, and every shot is in my head, and I’ve done the work, and I’ve done the homework, and I’m the A student. What if we did this?,’” Feste said. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, it was always the plan for feste’s stars to also sing their songs to add to the film’s deeper authenticity. “When I’m watching movies that feature performing artists, and there’s so much hype, and they’re playing this celebrated musical performer, and then they come on, and we hear them sing and we’re like, have they been re-voiced? Berdasarkan laporan, the pokémon day 2027 collection will be a nice little release to grab as fans of the franchise wait for pokémon day itself. #354. ’12 12 12′ Review: Anthony Mackie and Jamie Dornan’s Ticking-Clock Heist Thriller Runs on Broken Time

📅 13 Nov 2026

’12 12 12′ Review: Anthony Mackie and Jamie Dornan’s Ticking-Clock Heist Thriller Runs on Broken Time

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.indiewire.com/criticism/shows/12-12-12-review-apple-tv-series-heist-anthony-mackie-1235227284/

Diungkapkan bahwa every episode of “12 12 12” opens with the same explanation of its title: citing the fictitious law enforcement manual, “principles of crime, fbi research center, 4th edition,” anthony mackie explains, “a high asset robbery, professionally conceived, is 12 months in planning, 12 hours in execution. And then, we’re off to the races. A bank robber who’s not caught within 12 days is not caught at all. ” Then the screen splits horizontally to reveal images from the 12 months of preparation, the 12 hours of execution, and the 12 days when thief extraordinaire Paul Galvin (Jamie Dornan) does his best to elude Mackie’s obsessed FBI agent Jack Strickland. Related Stories ‘The Good Daughter’ Review: Rose Byrne Sizzles in Peacock’s Brutal Trauma-Drama About Crime-Solving Sisters ‘American Doctor’ and ‘You Can See Everything’ Lead 2027 Cinema Eye Honors Film Nominations.

Diungkapkan bahwa the heist genre, in theory, seems ripe for this kind of temporal manipulation. A game of wits between cops and criminals typically involves plenty of twists, many of which pull the rug out by flashing back to show where, when, and how it was placed so stealthily underfoot. Also working in “12 12 12’s” favor is the genre’s familiarity: There will be “getting the team together” montages, there will be unexpected hiccups in the days and hours during the robbery, there will be chest-thumping meetings between our confident cop and the equally confident con artist. Throw in the complex heist itself and the tense escape soon after, and there appear to be enough recognizable pieces that jumbling them up shouldn’t prove too confusing.

Sebagaimana diketahui, and “12 12 12” isn’t confusing. Taking a serpentine route through well-trodden territory does more to undermine our enjoyment of an otherwise well-mounted chase than it does to liven things up. It is, however, convoluted. They’re exciting in conception (when master thieves can wow us with their slick plans), they’re exciting to see carried out (when the shit hits the fan and even the most astute architects have to think on their feet), and they’re exciting to get away with (when safety is within reach, but it could be snatched away at any moment). Heists are inherently exciting. Anticipation, suspense, and anxiety work to form a natural arc, and disrupting that arc over and over, every hour for eight hours, in service of a few extra twists — and to extend what’s obviously a movie-length story across eight hours — simply isn’t worth it.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, on that note, let me get this minor but essential point out of the way now, quickly and clearly: jamie dornan needs more weird roles, not more conventional ones. We saw what he can do in “Barb and Star Go to Vista Del Mar” (a modern comedy classic). (Remember the bee movie?! No, not that bee movie — the other one. Let the man cook — or sing or dance or all three at once! He can do it! Honestly, I believe he can do anything. ).

Diungkapkan bahwa anyway, here his character’s only unique attribute is his brilliant… planning. Caught in a bind with his dumbass brother (Jack Kesy, doing his best Travis Kelce impression), Bobby lays it out in aptly blunt terms: “Paul, you’re the fucking plan guy, so plan me a plan. He’s got a mind for details, and he uses it to map out every possible contingency before embarking on his elaborate heists. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, but the only plans paul wants to make these days are for his family: he’s happy working on fishing boats off the coast of france and coming home to his wife, severine (agathe rousselle), in their little apartment above a bar. He’s bonded with his father-in-law, Serge (José Garcia), who’s the Marxist papa Paul never had, and he’s got a kid on the way.

Sebagaimana diketahui, unfortunately, bobby can’t stop being bobby and winds up indebted to the wrong people; people who don’t just want their money back, but who want more money to make up for the inconvenience. And since Bobby already owes more money than either brother could ever pay back, Paul has to take on one last job to free his brother — and himself — from their lives of crime.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, too bad that puts him back on jack’s radar or, i should say, squarely on jack’s radar, since jack is nursing a (secret) grudge against paul from years earlier. He wants revenge, he wants “respect,” he wants to win — “12 12 12” throws out a number of motivations for Jack early on that clearly don’t paint the full picture. Ever since, he’s been obsessed with catching the one criminal who’s eluded his grasp. They’re placeholder reasons until the show deems it time to dig into what’s really driving him to move to Zurich, hole up in a shitty police station, and wait for Paul to try to steal something.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, mackie, who’s reunited with his “falcon and the winter soldier” director kari skogland, gives great determined face, and dornan is the softest, sweetest guy on the fbi’s most-wanted list. (He doesn’t want to steal, but now that he must, he’s going to do it the right way. Thankfully, co-creators Dudi Appleton and Jim Keeble don’t ask their lead characters to betray their core identities amid all the twists and turns, shading Jack as more of an antagonist (all-consumed and, thus, single-minded to a fault) and Paul as more of the protagonist. ) That helps keep our rooting interests in line, which goes a long way toward a satisfying emotional payoff, even when the momentum ebbs and flows with every flash-forward, -back, and -sideways.

Diungkapkan bahwa with slick locations and clever-enough problem-solving, “12 12 12” should satisfy die-hard heist fans (but not “die hard’s” heist fans). It just takes a circuitous route to scratching that itch, and that’s almost as aggravating as not scratching it at all.

Berdasarkan laporan, “12 12 12” premieres friday, november 13 on apple tv with two episodes. New episodes will be released weekly through the finale (Episode 8) on December 25.

#363. Johnny Depp's Ebenezer Features One Character Most Adaptations Usually Cut

📅 13 Nov 2026

Johnny Depp's Ebenezer Features One Character Most Adaptations Usually Cut

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.slashfilm.com/2316683/johnny-depp-ebenezer-character-adaptations-cut-scrooge-sister/

Berdasarkan laporan, at this point in the life of charles dickens' 1843 novella "a christmas carol," so many stage and screen adaptations have been produced that the process of boiling the story down to its core elements has turned them into veritable tropes unto themselves. This aspect was being parodied as long ago as 1988's "Scrooged," which utilized an adaptation-within-an-adaptation as a bit of meta satire, as well as a commentary on how rote adapting Dickens' tale had become. Everything from a Victorian London setting to the line "God bless us, everyone" became not just quintessential to a new adaptation, but necessary, in much the same manner as the umpteenth cover of a popular song carries its own expectations. In a similar fashion to the elements which began to be regarded as a must-include, there were some other elements seen in Dickens' novella which got treated as unnecessary, and thus became more and more overlooked.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the most notable of these latter elements is the presence of a sister character for ebenezer scrooge. Yet Fan or her equivalent tends to be missing or altered in most modern adaptations. It would be erroneous to say that the sister is always cut from "A Christmas Carol" adaptations. This month's "Ebenezer," then, holds the honor of reinstating a sister character close to Dickens' Fan after a lengthy absence. After all, Fan Scrooge (as played by Carol Marsh) appears in one of the most revered film versions of the story, Brian Desmond Hurst's "A Christmas Carol" from 1951 starring Alistair Sim. She's nowhere in "Scrooged" or "The Muppet Christmas Carol," and she's heavily changed in the 2019 BBC miniseries starring Guy Pearce. While this is admirable, the reason for it doing so is due to the film's awkward revisionist take on Scrooge, as played by Johnny Depp.

Diungkapkan bahwa in "ebenezer" as in "a christmas carol," scrooge is reunited with his sister during his trip through his earlier years, courtesy of the ghost of christmas past (andrea riseborough). As in Dickens' novella, the sister is a fairly beatific figure, a protector of the bullied (and, it's heavily implied, abused by their father) Scrooge. In the film, screenwriter Nathaniel Halpern has renamed the sister from Fan to Molly (for what reason, only he knows), played by Rose Williams.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, on the one hand, one wonders why so many adaptations mess around with the character, considering how important she is to scrooge's nephew, fred (sam claflin). She's literally his mother, and the idea of Scrooge shunning Fred due to his discomfort over the untimely death of his beloved sister is a good source of dramatic tension.

Sebagaimana diketahui, yet on the other hand, it's likely that most adaptations either reconfigure or leave the sister out because her presence exists to humanize scrooge in a way that some adaptations would rather not deal with. The sister and her fleshing out of Scrooge's origin story, as it were, forces the character to be more nuanced. Of course, most intelligent audience members should be able to understand that a young victim turned adult monster doesn't mean his misdeeds are automatically forgiven, yet those who think of "A Christmas Carol" primarily as a story for young children might.

Berdasarkan laporan, in any case, "ebenezer" corrects this error too far the other way, adding to it some other odd changes which make scrooge a little too sympathetic. At least director Ti West and company don't let him completely off the hook, either, but it's too bad that the sister is re-included in the film for little more reason than as a character witness.

Berdasarkan laporan, it hasn't been an easy time for marvel studios of late, but if anyone can get the franchise back on track, it's surely the avengers (well, them and the box office behemoth that was "spider-man: brand new day"). "Avengers: Doomsday" is almost upon us, but the titular roster looks a lot different in 2026 than it did when "The Avengers" debuted back in 2012. Now, Marvel has officially confirmed who will stand beside Anthony Mackie's Sam Wilson/Captain America in the upcoming team-up movie.

Diungkapkan bahwa marvel studios announced the full "doomsday" cast some time ago, but there's been some confusion about who counts as an avenger, ever since the tumultuous events of "captain america: civil war. So, who is still considered part of the official Avengers roster?.

Diungkapkan bahwa otherwise, the team is looking much different to the og lineup, which started out with steve rogers/captain america, thor, scarlett johansson's natasha romanoff/black widow, mark ruffalo's bruce banner/hulk, robert downey jr. Of course, RDJ will be back as Doctor Doom in "Doomsday," but Marvel has seemingly confirmed he won't be playing a Tony Stark variant and will, in fact, portray an entirely separate character in Victor Von Doom. 's Tony Stark/Iron Man, and Jeremy Renner's Clint Barton/Hawkeye. That means the only original member in "Doomsday" will be Thor, and if he's fully welcomed back into the fold, Steve Rogers.

Berdasarkan laporan, meanwhile, for anthony mackie, this is all a chance to showcase himself as the true leader of the latest avengers lineup. "In 'Endgame,' Steve gave him the shield and said, 'You need to be the leader of the Avengers,'" he told Empire. "Now you get to see more of him leading the charge with everyone into battle. ".

Diungkapkan bahwa whether the avengers roster will change by the end of "doomsday" or its planned follow-up, "avengers: secret wars" remains to be seen (there's bound to be some cameos at least). For now, we know who's heading into battle against Doom alongside the new Cap.

#370. 7 Sci-Fi Shows Fans Either Love Or Hate

📅 13 Nov 2026

7 Sci-Fi Shows Fans Either Love Or Hate

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://screenrant.com/sci-fi-shows-fans-love-or-hate/

Berdasarkan laporan, sci-fi tv shows are notoriously difficult to get right. The idea of a universally beloved science fiction series is basically a myth. Even the most celebrated sci-fi shows have detractors who are every bit as vocal as their supporters. The genre’s fandom can be fickle, and even the grandest ideas or most impressive visual spectacle cannot guarantee a series will succeed. However, some sci-fi shows take that divide to another level, earning reputations as timeless masterpieces and embarrassing low points in almost the same breath.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, these aren’t shows that are so bad they become entertaining, either. When it gets interesting is with the shows that have a strong premise and something substantial to offer, whether that’s inventive storytelling, memorable characters, or a fresh approach to an established universe. It’s understandable when a deliberately B-Movie-style sci-fi series splits the genre’s fandom down the middle. Their most controversial qualities are often precisely what their admirers treasure, making their divisive nature almost as fascinating as the sci-fi stories they tell.

Berdasarkan laporan, few shows demand such an immediate leap of faith as the oa. Its story begins with Prairie Johnson (Brit Marling), a previously blind woman who returns after disappearing for seven years, now able to see. The whole thing is incredibly surreal both conceptually and visually, and for The OA’s fans, the rejection of conventional storytelling is the attraction. What follows combines near-death experiences, alternate dimensions, and characters that can supposedly transcend ordinary reality. The series treats belief and human connection with an earnestness that makes its strangest developments feel emotionally meaningful, even when their mechanics can’t really be explained.

Diungkapkan bahwa however, that prioritizing of emotional sincerity makes the oa difficult viewing for anyone who cannot accept its central concepts and premise. The dialogue sometimes tries a little too hard to be profound, and its mysteries require a lot of patience before offering anything resembling clarity. Where fans see a sci-fi show brave enough to let viewers have their own interpretation of what’s happening, skeptics see The OA as a series that mistakes obscurity for depth.

Berdasarkan laporan, continuing the story of a celebrated graphic novel as a tv show was always going to provoke disagreement, especially when that graphic novel is alan moore’s watchmen. HBO’s series moves the action to an alternate 2019, where masked police officers confront a white supremacist organization in Tulsa. Detective Angela Abar (Regina King) becomes the center of a mystery connecting racial violence and the concealed history of costumed heroes, all of which is underpinned by an exploration of inherited trauma. Fans praised the show for finding fresh relevance in its source material, but many viewers had a much less positive response.

Sebagaimana diketahui, many viewers openly disliked the heavy emphasis hbo’s watchmen placed on american racism, while others find the treatment of legacy characters like dr. Few critical voices found flaws in the show as a TV series. The disagreement ultimately concerns what a continuation owes its predecessor. Manhattan and Ozymandius completely missed the point of Alan Moore’s original story. Fans loved the way HBO’s Watchmen used the world of the graphic novel to explore contemporary social anxieties, while those who loved the source material completely rejected the way it used the world of Watchmen as a vehicle to make a political statement.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in theory, an alien invasion should lead to a high-octane, action-packed sci-fi story. Following people across different countries as extraterrestrial forces arrive, the series emphasizes personal grief, and the confusion of experiencing a catastrophe without understanding its scale rather than grand spectacle. Apple TV’s Invasion, however, takes a deliberately different approach, and it turned pit to be a polarizing one. The threat of the invasion still feels enormous, but it’s due to the characters' responses to what’s going on rather than any kind of grand explosive display of advanced alien technology. Some people loved this unique approach to an alien invasion narrative, but others very much didn’t.

Sebagaimana diketahui, for invasion’s detractors, the slow-burn of the unfolding catastrophe felt like a stalled narrative. The focus on grounded moments like domestic arguments or panic attacks occupied a lot of narrative space without doing much to make the characters more compelling. The show’s perspective is an interesting idea, but an interesting idea doesn’t make up for bad pacing. Those invested in its atmosphere appreciate living through uncertainty alongside the characters experience it, but viewers waiting for meaningful developments feel that Invasion keeps postponing the story its premise promised.

Berdasarkan laporan, for some fans, star trek: discovery brought urgency and emotional openness to a franchise that needed to evolve. Discovery as they navigate a radically unfamiliar future. Its admirers praise its cinematic presentation, inclusive ensemble cast, and insistence that compassion remains meaningful under extreme pressure. Centering on Michael Burnham (Sonequa Martin-Green), it follows the crew of the U. S. S. Rather than presenting optimism as an uncomplicated starting point like many Star Trek shows, Discovery frequently makes its characters struggle toward it, giving their commitment to cooperation a personal intensity that resonates strongly with its audience.

Sebagaimana diketahui, this intensity is exactly why star trek: discovery is perhaps the most polarizing star trek show so far. Burnham’s repeated importance to enormous crises also makes the wider universe feel unusually dependent on a single character, a trait that feels much closer to Star Wars than it does Trek. Its season-long emergencies leave less room for exploratory adventures-of-the-week, while leaning into emotional speeches often interrupts situations that demand immediate action. Essentially, Discovery created intense debates around what a Star Trek series should prioritize, and the discussion still rages on two years after it concluded.

Diungkapkan bahwa the appeal of rick & morty extends beyond increasingly elaborate sci-fi jokes. It’s a series that moves from grotesque sic-if flavored slapstick to existential despair with remarkable speed. The adventures of its central duo use grand concepts like multiversal travel as ways to explore deep psychological problems, such as if alternate realities make family members replaceable or if scientific genius justifies rejecting emotional attachment. Rick & Morty fans see this versatility as its greatest strength. It’s capable of mocking sci-fi’s absurdity while also finding genuine emotional depth in the implications of the genre’s grandest concepts.

Berdasarkan laporan, the problem for those on the other side of the fence is that rick & morty is seen as a series that insists upon itself. For those that hate it, the belching, gore, sexual jokes, and gratuitousness are the series true identity, and capping off an episode with a moment or two of philosophical insight doesn’t change this. Not only that, but the show’s nihilistic approach to narrative consequences makes it impossible to ever truly care about Rick, Morty, or any other character, according to some. Ultimately, Rick & Morty is a show filled with emotional contradictions, and this seems central to both its appeal and the frustration it inspires.

Diungkapkan bahwa set roughly a century before the phantom menace, the acolyte had an unusually promising opportunity to explore a relatively untouched period in the star wars timeline. Fans of The Acolyte immediately praised both the distance from the Skywalker saga and the Disney+ Star Wars show’s willingness to question the Jedi’s confidence in their own judgment. An investigation into attacks on Jedi gradually exposes buried wrongdoing and, eventually, some major flaws in the order’s central philosophy. However, an intriguing premise does not automatically produce a great sci-fi TV show.

Sebagaimana diketahui, even beyond those who didn’t appreciate the jedi being portrayed at their most fallible, plenty of people hated the acolyte for what they viewed as awkward dialogue, uneven pacing, and difficult-to-understand character decisions. For The Acolyte’s admirers, its storytelling flaws are easy to look past thanks to it being a worthwhile expansion of the franchise’s moral tapestry. There were plenty of complaints that had nothing to do with the show’s reframing of Jedi history. For others, the show is a flawed execution of ideas that are far less complex than they claim to be, leaving a potentially compelling mystery sidelined by an attempt to unnecessarily upend Star Wars canon.

Sebagaimana diketahui, while the story that followed became incredibly divisive, it's almost universally agreed that lost’s central premise of plane crash survivors awakening on an island filled with impossible phenomena is exceptionally solid. Lost turns its setup into an expansive mystery box drama about damaged people confronting circumstances they cannot explain. Flashbacks give seemingly straightforward conflicts unexpected emotional weight, while the island’s secrets make almost every discovery feel significant. It’s what the show does with that idea that makes it one of the most polarizing sci-fi shows ever made. For the first few seasons, this was enough. However, as Lost went on, the cracks in viewer responses started to show.

Berdasarkan laporan, in many ways, lost created this problem for itself by inviting viewers to scrutinize every detail. Over a decade after it concluded, that division remains. Those that loved the show were happy with how the dots joined up. It created expectations about how those details would eventually connect. For some viewers, Lost is one of the greatest sci-fi shows ever made. Those that didn’t either hate the end result, or simply grew sick of the constant drip-feed of mysteries with comparatively few tangible answers. The finale of Lost crystallized that disagreement by prioritizing emotional reunion over clearly explaining what the island is and how it worked. For others, it’s a reason to be mad at ABC for hours of viewing they’re never going to get back.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the hundred thousand kingdoms is the first book in n. Jemisin's The Inheritance Trilogy, followed by The Broken Kingdoms and The Kingdom of the Gods. Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, finally, sanderson recommends "anything by robin hobb, but particularly the fitz books," referring to hobb's 16-book series the realm of the elderlings. #373. Blizzard Officially Responds to Disappointed Overwatch Fans Over Hero 55

📅 13 Nov 2026

Blizzard Officially Responds to Disappointed Overwatch Fans Over Hero 55

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.polygon.com/overwatch-new-hero-55-hudson-damage-dps-blizzard/

Hero 55 was supposed to bring some Omnic aura to the Support roster; things have changed.

Sebagaimana diketahui, blizzard entertainment is about to make good on the promise of delivering 10 new heroes to overwatch in 2026, with the final addition arriving in december. The 10th new hero coming to Overwatch in 2026 is an Omnic detective named Hudson, and he'll arrive alongside the launch of season 6. Hudson was officially revealed on Thursday, but many Overwatch fans aren't pleased with a key aspect of his character.

Originally pitched as a new Support hero for Overwatch, Hudson will instead be part of the hero shooter's Damage (DPS) roster.

Sebagaimana diketahui, overwatch game director aaron keller and associate director alec dawson discussed the new hero — the game's 55th overall — during a video interview with creators emongg and flats, where the two revealed the character's name and role change. Keller called the role switch a late-in-development "pivot. ".

Berdasarkan laporan, "as the hero developed, as we look at the mechanics, how they match with the aesthetic, how they match with who the hero is supposed to be, how they’re supposed to be represented in our game, season 6’s hero will be a dps," dawson explained. "He's really fun. ".

Berdasarkan laporan, dawson added, "during development, we iterated a lot, we playtested a lot, and the core mechanic and the thing that we were really falling in love with on this hero didn’t really match with being a support. So we’re really excited for him pretty soon. We kind of leaned into the things we loved the most about the hero, and it definitely fit DPS a lot better. ".

Diungkapkan bahwa overwatch players who wanted a new support hero were less excited to learn that they weren't getting the cool omnic detective they were promised. Some called it a "bait and switch. " Overwatch currently has 23 damage heroes. Hudson will be the 24th.

Berdasarkan laporan, on friday, keller responded to backlash about hudson's place on the overwatch roster, offering more context on the decision to "help players understand it, even as some of them are disappointed. ".

Berdasarkan laporan, "when we started work on the detective, he was a support," keller said in a thread on x. "But as time went on and the kit continued development we realized that it wasn’t working. Once we tested Hudson as a DPS, the turn around in our feelings for him was instantaneous and dramatic.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "this decision ultimately wasn't whether we release a dps or a support hero, it was whether we release a great character or one we didn't believe in. Game dev isn’t always straightforward. I hope you all feel the same way when he launches in Season 6. Sometimes we need to adapt to create the best version of something. Building Heroes for OW is as much of an art form as a technical challenge. The team is incredibly proud of this Hero. ".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, overwatch season 6 is expected to arrive on tuesday, dec. 8.

Blizzard's ambitious plan to release 10 heroes this year may never be repeated, but seasonal releases are sticking.

Diungkapkan bahwa kelly embodied the mysterious aura that her admirers associated with her astrological sign. Unfortunately, that light was extinguished on September 14, 1982, when the Princess of Monaco lost her life in a tragic car accident on the hills above the principality.

Diungkapkan bahwa per flixpatrol, not only have both chapters been in the paramount+ charts for over a month, until november 13, 2026, "chapter one" was sitting at the very top of the u. movie charts, with "Chapter Two" occupying the second spot. Russell Brand was charged with rape and sexual assault in April 2025.

Russell Brand pleaded not guilty to all charges.

Russell Brand was found guilty of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in a november 2026 ruling, a london court found brand guilty of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault. He was cleared of two additional counts of rape and one count of indecent assault.

During the trial, Brand maintained his innocence and said that while he dedicated much of his life to “beyond reckless philandering,” per the New York Times, he never engaged in non-consensual activities.

#380. Doctor Who Star Peter Capaldi Knows How To Save The Struggling Sci-Fi Series

📅 13 Nov 2026

Doctor Who Star Peter Capaldi Knows How To Save The Struggling Sci-Fi Series

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.slashfilm.com/2313324/doctor-who-star-peter-capaldi-how-save-sci-fi-series/

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, as "doctor who" fans (aka whovians) are no doubt aware, the show is in a bit of a bind. The character, you see, is a time-traveling alien known as a Time Lord, and when they die, they're able to regenerate into a new person. Since its debut way back in 1963, the series has sustained itself with a clever sci-fi concept that has allowed multiple actors to canonically play the title role of the Doctor. Each time the Doctor regenerates, their personality changes a bit, although they still have the same memories, intellect, and enthusiasm.

Sebagaimana diketahui, unfortunately, after running for so long, "doctor who" has developed a bad habit of falling back on stale tropes. A Whovian friend of mine has agreed that "Doctor Who" is in a bad place right now, and the franchise's future is uncertain in the wake of Disney ending its partnership with the show due to its relatively low viewership. As my friend put it, the series is, indeed, in a "tepid" place, and no one knows where it will go moving forward.

Berdasarkan laporan, peter capaldi, however, has some suggestions. The actor, who played the Twelfth Doctor from 2014 to 2017, shared his ideas during his recent appearance on the "Half the Picture" podcast, explaining that he thinks the show needs to get back to basics. He added that it would do well to reorient itself by returning to its lower budgeted origins and tapping back into the shoddy charms of its earliest days.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in the same interview, peter capaldi clarified that he is fine with no longer being associated with "doctor who," as there are other ventures he would like to pursue. "Doctor Who," he noted, is the kind of show that takes over your life, adding, "You can't do it [. ] as a part-time role. " When it comes to the property's future, though, Capaldi is uncertain, stating:.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "what it's got to be, i don't know. That's what I grew up with. I was thinking about this [. ' I mean, 'Doctor Who' has always had ambition, it's just that budgets haven't always met that. Because my love for the show was the old show. Let's make it black-and-white with very wobbly sets. Or with less ambition. And that's not going to work. ] I don't know what people want from it. Let's make more cheaply. I can't come in and say 'Let's set it in the '60s. ".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, capaldi then mused out loud if audiences might want "david and kylie. Or maybe they're more interested in previous "Doctor Who" stars like Christopher Eccleston or Jodie Whitaker. " He was, of course, referring to David Tennant's highly popular iteration of the Doctor appearing with a character played by Kylie Minogue on "Doctor Who" in the 2007 Christmas special "Voyage of the Damned" (which brought in an impressive number of viewers). Basically, Capaldi is very unsure what fans really want out of the series.

Sebagaimana diketahui, all he can say is that he enjoys "doctor who" the best when it experiences what he calls a "ripple" from the old show. Not a reused monster, necessarily, but a specific tone that sometimes breaks through. Something humble and old-fashioned.

Sebagaimana diketahui, although "doctor who" is a time-travel series that involves aliens, monsters, major historical figures, and ineffable, universe-ending technologies, peter capaldi feels that it's actually a "small" show. It's about a small group of characters and their time-traveling TARDIS, which looks like a police box that, via advanced technology, is larger on the inside than on the outside. Capaldi added that if the series could focus on those basics, it could sing once again, explaining:.

Diungkapkan bahwa "it's the doctor and the assistant-slash-assistants in the tardis. And like in 'The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe,' they step out the door to this drama. Quite contained. Magical, strange, weird, sad. It's that central core of that small group of people with the Doctor at the center of it. And those dramas change shape, and they've got monsters in them. Kind of balming. ".

Diungkapkan bahwa i have personally watched enough of the show to know that most of the best "doctor who" episodes embody what capaldi talked about. The problem, then, is that many of the series' seasonal storylines climax with some sort of supervillain threatening to destroy the universe, unwrite history, or commit some other kind of massive sci-fi cataclysm. And if those types of cataclysms are regularly happening, then it's no surprise that fans are experiencing a sense of fatigue (or that the show's creatives may be running low on ideas).

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, time will tell if the minds currently behind "doctor who" take capaldi's advice and scale the series back into a cheaper, more humble form. It certainly wouldn't hurt, what with the series being adrift following its short-lived Disney era and the planned 2026 Christmas special being canceled. Capaldi might just be onto something.

Diungkapkan bahwa the dinosaurs themselves are magnificent, rendered with the feathers and fuzzy hair that we now know dinosaurs sported without losing the fearsome nature imbued by spielberg 30 years ago. This is a movie where dinosaurs repeatedly slaughter and eat random humans, and each kill got an applause from my theater's rowdy audience every time. Mitchell and his team also take some creative swings with the creature designs that largely pay off, including a family of large rocky turtles and a terrifying silent serpent as long as a train with rows of impossibly sharp teeth.

Diungkapkan bahwa heartland is one of the strangest movies in jessica chastain’s career. The Oscar-winner plays Misty Jones, a former country megastar who returns home to Nashville to investigate the sudden disappearance of her niece, Charlie Hart, who’s following in her footsteps as a country musician.

Sebagaimana diketahui, being heumann is based on judy heumann's memoir, "being heumann: an unrepentant memoir of a disability rights activist," dramatizing the 28-day sit-in protest at the san francisco federal building by disability activists. The demonstration led to the first U. S. federal civil rights protections for people with disabilities.

Berdasarkan laporan, ron howard’s most recent film is a documentary centered on richard avedon, one of the most important photographers in fashion history. The film has great access to Avedon’s personal files, showing never-before-seen images and interviews with family members and figures like Twiggy, Isabella Rossellini, and more.

Berdasarkan laporan, misty green follows a once-successful actress and performer whose career has been derailed due to addiction, self-sabotage, and an evolving, challenging industry. After facing challenges from all sides, Misty goes on a desperate job hunt, pursuing a starring role in a remake of the musical Dreamgirls.

Sebagaimana diketahui, heart of the beast follows brad pitt as a traumatized soldier who gets stranded in the alaskan wilderness alongside his combat-trained german shepard. The two band together to survive and return to civilization.

Sebagaimana diketahui, two isolated middle-aged siblings' lives (gayle rankin and grant o’rourke) are disrupted when they receive an eviction notice from the government. Raised to view all outsiders as threats, the siblings are shocked by the arrival of a mild-mannered land recovery coordinator (Domhnall Gleeson), who doesn’t know how to communicate with them.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, pan’s labyrinth is a special film in guillermo del toro’s filmography, and his most direct exploration of fairy tales. The series is set in the aftermath of the Spanish Civil War and follows Ofelia (Ivana Baquero), a 12-year-old girl who’s just moved to a military outpost managed by her terrifying stepfather (Sergi Lopez). She uncovers a rich fantasy world after stumbling upon a labyrinth and a faun, who informs her that she’s the reincarnation of a Princess and must complete three tasks to return to her kingdom.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, after terrifying everyone with its amazing trailer, other mommy is finally available on streaming. The film follows Bela (Arabella Olivia Clark), the daughter of parents who are going through a marital crisis. She starts to form a relationship with a malignant shapeshifting entity that calls itself Other Mommy.

Sebagaimana diketahui, v/h/s mixtape is the latest entry in the vhs franchise, a found-footage horror anthology that has featured directors like ti west, adam wingard, scott derrickson, and more. This year’s version is centered on the music industry and framed in the style of an MTV news show.

Johnny Depp’s ‘Ebenezer’ Makes a Weak Case for His Post-Trial Comeback

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.vanityfair.com/story/ebenezer-johnny-depp-comeback

Sebagaimana diketahui, for weeks, los angeles has been plastered with posters of a malevolent-looking man in a top hat and gray sideburns. It always takes me a few minutes to process that this elderly curmudgeon is Johnny Depp, doing his Hollywood walk of shame in Ebenezer.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “it’s good to be back,” depp gurgles in the movie’s trailer. He’s either reveling in his return from infamy or trolling the audience, depending on your point of view.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i adored johnny depp back in his edward scissorhands/gilbert grape/ed wood heyday; he probably would’ve been my hall pass if i’d known about the concept back then. Now, though, it feels as if the once chiseled-cheeked heartthrob has found a character that suits him: a monstrous figure seeking redemption.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “grant me the grace to prove that i am no longer the man that i once was,” ebenezer scrooge begs one of the ghosts haunting him in this rather plodding new version of charles dickens’s a christmas carol, directed by horror auteur ti west. Scrooge is trying to make up for a lifetime of stinginess and cruelty, whereas Depp seeks to win back mainstream audiences after the ugly, drawn-out brawl that was his marriage and divorce from Amber Heard.

Sebagaimana diketahui, heard alleged that he was an abusive addict. Depp denied abusing her and filed two defamation suits. He aimed one at the British tabloid The Sun for calling him a wife-beater (which he lost, since the court found the characterization to be “substantially true”). The other was leveled at Heard for describing herself in a Washington Post op-ed as “a public figure representing domestic abuse. ” What started as a defamation trial ended up as a livestreamed referendum on post-#MeToo gender politics.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the saga spawned organized smear campaigns soaked in misogyny. It seemed to echo one of Depp’s texts about Heard, released during the trial, in which he proposed to a friend: “Let’s drown her before we burn her!!!…I will fuck her burnt corpse afterwards to make sure she is dead. Social media erupted with vile memes, hashtags, and videos targeting Heard, bearing hashtags like #AmberHeardIsAPsychopath and #DontBelieveAllWomen. ” And it wasn’t just ordinary guys taking up arms for Depp. One men’s group launched a “Ditch the Witch” protest in support of Depp. Moments after the verdict was announced, the GOP’s House Judiciary tweeted a GIF of Depp in Pirates of the Caribbean from its official account, showing support for him.

Berdasarkan laporan, “the craziness [aimed at heard] was a kind of pent-up anger at women,” a film producer suggested to me back in 2022. “I think it really stirred up a lot of deep-seated resentment that hasn’t been allowed expression since #MeToo. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, depp didn’t come out of the crucible with his career intact. Still, he never really went away. In fact, like so many guys who have been supposedly “canceled,” he wormed his way back in quite easily. The next year, he directed the movie Modì, Three Days on the Wing of Madness. He was asked to resign from the Fantastic Beasts franchise—though Warner Bros. Meanwhile, producer Jerry Bruckheimer confirmed in 2025 that he’s been talking to Depp about a sixth Pirates film after all. still paid Depp his full $16 million salary—and his former agent claimed Disney dropped him from the next Pirates of the Caribbean movie. In 2023, he got a standing ovation at Cannes for his role as Louis XV in the French film Jeanne du Barry. All the while, Depp has also kept his massive brand deal as the face of Dior’s Sauvage.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “i don’t feel boycotted by hollywood because i don’t think about hollywood,” depp announced imperiously a few years back. ” Enter Ebenezer, his official return to…Hollywood. “I don’t have much further need for Hollywood. Which he doesn’t need or think about. At all.

Sebagaimana diketahui, call it christmas-washing: what could be more wholesome and uncontroversial than a christmas carol? according to variety, paramount paid depp just $5 million—a big drop-off from the days when he could reportedly command $50 million for a single film—and only spent $38 million to produce the movie, hedging its bets. Still, this film is a pretty warm welcome back to American movie screens, major marketing campaign and all.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, unfortunately, depp’s mediocre performance in ebenezer doesn’t dispel the sour scent of desperation that hangs over his career. Scrooge is one of the most unlovable characters in all of literature, and Depp’s charm does not shine through the gnarled facial prosthetics. Depp’s inspiration for the role might as well have been Oscar the Grouch, though one with less educational value who’s hollow at his core. He plays the archetypal miser in the broadest of ways, spending much of the nearly two-hour movie alternating between exaggerated expressions of cantankerousness and horror. At various points, the actor campily throws himself into physical comedy that is at odds with the horror-soaked vibe of West’s production.

Sebagaimana diketahui, knowing this is a test run for depp’s uncanceling, viewers will find it hard not to see ebenezer as a wink-filled plea for absolution. “Allow me my redemption. “I’m not the man I was!” his character screams over and over. ” To which the answer—or my answer, at least—is simple: Bah, humbug.
