Diungkapkan bahwa of all the movies in 2026 that can claim to be the timeliest, none may have a better case than "how to rob a bank. " Even setting aside the obvious social and political commentary behind director David Leitch's newest heist flick, in which a group of Robin Hood-like bank robbers team up to send a message to corporate bigwigs and capitalist vultures, the movie's timeliness is also apparent in the way it's shot and edited. The various trailers have made no secret of the content creator angle behind this crew, led by Nicholas Hoult's Ryan (aka The Wolf). When they're not sticking up banks and making thrilling getaways, they're busy editing their escapades into viral-ready YouTube videos to be consumed by the masses.

Sebagaimana diketahui, it's a novel approach that'll either work or not for audiences, many of whom are well aware of the online ecosystem that is influencer culture. During a recent press junket for the film, I spoke to both Leitch and producing partner Kelly McCormick about the deep well of influences they drew from in order to nail this specific element of the film — one that certainly attempts to feel true to our digital lives. It's a tall task for any mainstream Hollywood movie to tackle, but the creative team behind "How to Rob a Bank" clearly did their homework. According to McCormick:.

Diungkapkan bahwa "we were trying to go for what might be the next push for creators, if you know what i mean. Like, the wish fulfillment aspect from a creator's perspective of just pushing the envelope even more. So it was just really absorbing as much as possible to see what was out there and then using some of the prosumer cameras to make sure that we were just being even more wild. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, the content creator footage depicted throughout "how to rob a bank" will inevitably leave an impression. (Not yet, at least. No, we don't live in a world where adrenaline-seeking influencers actually put themselves and others in harm's way to pull off successful heists and robberies. ) But actually capturing those vibes in an authentic way meant resorting to some very specific filmmaking measures.

Sebagaimana diketahui, one scene shows ryan and his friends fleeing the scene of the crime on motorcycles through a forest, with gopros strapped to their helmets capturing footage in every direction. When this is filtered through the lens of the video they upload afterwards, well, that's where things get visually dynamic. As Kelly McCormick explained to me:.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "the one [scene] in specific i always remember is when they're biking through the forest and you see it from above and we are pivoting the camera in editorial, because literally it's capturing [360 degrees] around [the action]. And so you can spin it around in editorial to get that vibe of this wild editing that I think would be a creator's dream, if they didn't have to hit deadlines and always be feeding as much as possible to their hungry, hungry followers [laughs]. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, david leitch name-checks "extreme sports" as one section of youtube they paid particular attention to for sequences like that, while the idea of philanthropy and giving back to communities was taken out of the mr. Even podcasters get into the mix, like Scott Galloway or King Bach (both of whom make cameos in the film). Beast playbook. Adds Leitch with a laugh, "We had a lot of influences in our influencers. ".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the odyssey, one of the highest-grossing films of the 2026 movie schedule, is a serious movie that blends mythological themes and modern storytelling as it explores the journey of odysseus as he faces a dangerous voyage through fantastical realms on his way back to his family. And its director, Christopher Nolan, is a revered filmmaker known for paying attention to little details as he brings his signature narrative and visual style to life on the big screen. That doesn’t mean hilarious behind-the-scenes moments and shenanigans don’t still happen during production, and one in particular involves Tom Holland requesting skirt alterations.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the fantasy epic marked tom holland’s first time working with the filmmaker, and boy does he have some memorable stories to share from the experience. For example, according to Variety, who was at the November 10 FYC event, the current Spider-Man decided to take matters of his skirt into his own hands with costume designer Ellen Mirojnick, asking her to hem it to help give him some height on screen.

Berdasarkan laporan, in the 75-minute documentary behind the scenes of the odyssey, chronicling the making of the three-hour blockbuster, holland revealed that his reasoning for the change didn’t matter because you can’t sneak anything by christopher nolan. He said:.

I asked Ellen, the costume designer, I said, ‘Could you just make the skirt a little shorter?’ It’ll make me look a little taller.

Estimated to fall somewhere between 5’6” and 5’8”, I can absolutely understand wanting to appear as tall as possible while starring in such a big movie.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i also appreciate that the peter parker actor has enough self-awareness to make such a request. Apparently, he even got the request fulfilled when the costume designer had his tailored skirt ready six weeks later. However, Christopher Nolan noticed that something was amiss and had the following question:.

Two seconds into taking in the costume, [Christopher Nolan] was like, ‘How come the skirt is shorter?’.

Diungkapkan bahwa critics heaped praise on the odyssey, and the box office numbers reflected that audiences couldn’t get enough, so the length of tom holland’s skirt clearly had no effect on the ultimate outcome. But personally, I now wish I knew what the actor’s response was when the Inception director asked what happened. Did he cop to his attempt to look taller on screen? Did he try to play it off in some other way? Did the filmmaker find it as hilarious as I do?.

Without a camera turned on them both in that moment, we might never know for sure, but I’m not surprised that someone as meticulous as Christopher Nolan noticed almost immediately and called out the change.

Diungkapkan bahwa there have already been plenty of memorable stories about the shoot, as matt damon talked about being “wet” and “cold” during portions of the production while charlize theron acted through massive winds that got up to 30 to 40 miles per hour. Now, I hope we get more silly tales like this one from Tom Holland.

Sebagaimana diketahui, with the odyssey expected to be a major awards contender this year, i feel like that's very possible. So, here's hoping we get to learn more about Tom Holland trying to shorten his skirt for this Christopher Nolan epic.

#394. Johnny Depp's Ebenezer Makes An Alarming Change To The Story Of A Christmas Carol

📅 13 Nov 2026

Johnny Depp's Ebenezer Makes An Alarming Change To The Story Of A Christmas Carol

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.slashfilm.com/2315819/johnny-depp-ebenezer-a-christmas-carol-story-change/

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, when the ads and pre-release buzz articles began running for "ebenezer," the new film directed by ti west and starring johnny depp as scrooge, the campaign promised that the movie would present charles dickens' "a christmas carol" as you'd never seen it before. The movie liberally copy-and-pastes whole swathes of Dickens' text into the script, with writer Nathaniel Halpern even bothering to include the novella's separation into five staves. Yet, now that the film has released and folks (including yours truly) have screened it, it turns out "Ebenezer" is unsurprisingly more or less the same "A Christmas Carol" we all know well. However, it seems there's some larger artistic liberty wiggle room in that "more or less the same" than might appear at first glance.

Sebagaimana diketahui, when west spoke to entertainment weekly back in august, he detailed what made depp's ebenezer different than previous adaptations. Amidst talking up things like Depp's "musicality" as a performer, West also explained how his film would present Scrooge in a more both sides-y manner: "As [Depp's] Scrooge cuts someone down verbally or as he makes a financial point or withdraws, you do understand why he's doing it. " That offhand mention of "a financial point" baffled many of us when we first read it, as it certainly did sound like a deviation from Dickens.

Diungkapkan bahwa was this scrooge going to be portrayed as a genius businessman? instead, the changes "ebenezer" makes to scrooge and dickens' story are of a smaller nature. They involve portraying a couple small supporting characters as outright villains, thereby giving Scrooge a justification for his misanthropy. The changes may be merely tweaks, yet their larger implications are alarming, especially for a film which doesn't feel able to support them.

Diungkapkan bahwa for the most part, "ebenezer" is a faithful adaptation of "a christmas carol. Marley goes to get some tea while Scrooge observes a beggar outside his window. " The largest addition comes in the form of a prologue in which we see Scrooge and his partner, Jacob Marley (Ian McKellen), on their last day together. At the same moment the beggar reveals himself to Scrooge as a fraud conning people out of their donations, Marley drops dead, equating the con artist's crime with harm done to a true earner in Scrooge's mind. That Marley (and Scrooge) are just as heartless and dishonest is something the film hopes Dickens' work gets across, as they don't go out of their way to underline it to support their addition.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, this problem is compounded twice. Once is when it's revealed that Scrooge's old benevolent boss Fezziwig was murdered by a street beggar, further teaching Scrooge that charity can be met with violence. Next is when the Ghost of Christmas Future shows Scrooge the vultures who've come to sully his legacy after his death, which adds the wrinkle that the two men who sought a donation for the poor at the beginning of the film are actually also embezzlers.

Sebagaimana diketahui, what's more, they're in league with a man who's plotting with the embezzlers to steal scrooge's nephew fred's inheritance with the production of a forged will. The alarming quality about these inclusions lies in how they seem to give Scrooge more moral justification for his odious behavior that he doesn't need. It's a bizarrely tone-deaf addition for a story that's ultimately meant to be about the virtues of charity.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, ultimately (and thankfully), these additions do not derail "ebenezer," for the heart of charles dickens' story and his themes remains intact. Although it's tempting to point fingers at the Skydance corporation for the new ideas, it isn't the changes themselves that are the problem. "Ebenezer" is indeed partially constructed to emphasize the horror in Dickens' tale: the three Christmas ghosts are more ghastly and doomed than they typically are. After all, Ti West comes from a background of indie horror films, many of which utilize thorny, morally ambiguous characterizations and themes as their stock in trade. In the more horror-centric version of "A Christmas Carol" the movie seems to want to be, a somewhat justified Scrooge would be a fascinating layer for an actor to play, as it creates a new obstacle for the character to overcome on his journey to selflessness.

Sebagaimana diketahui, alas, "ebenezer" is the johnny depp show, and for several reasons, depp is not up to the task. Instead, "Ebenezer" and Depp are too preoccupied with trying to be as likable as possible, which means that his Scrooge rarely gets nasty. He comes off more like an irritable jerk than a man who's nearly lost his soul, so whatever compelling shadings the changes to the story could've presented never materialize. While it's arguable that he may not be able to tackle such material at all, it seems like he's not even interested in trying in the first place. On paper, the possibilities presented by "Ebenezer" range from exciting to alarming. Yet we needn't fret too much, since the finished film plays things so safely that it's hard to get riled up about it one way or the other.

#396. 3 Best Sci-Fi Books To Read This Weekend (November 14-15)

📅 13 Nov 2026

3 Best Sci-Fi Books To Read This Weekend (November 14-15)

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://collider.com/best-sci-fi-books-read-this-weekend-november-14/

Sebagaimana diketahui, science fiction is among the most popular genres around, and for good reason. Rich in worldbuilding and dealing with themes of oppression, ambition, liberation, and the advancement of the human race, sci-fi is an enduring part of most media, but it's especially prominent in literature. Ever since Mary Shelley's foundational classic, Frankenstein, came out, the genre has kept growing until it became the juggernaut it is today.

Sebagaimana diketahui, today, sci-fi is incredibly prolific, and you can find at least one book about every single possible subgenre, tackling every possible angle. If you're in the mood for a riveting sci-fi book to read this weekend, then look no further than the ones on this list. One of these you can probably start and finish over the weekend, and the others might take a bit longer. However, they're all incredible choices for you to tackle come Saturday morning.

Berdasarkan laporan, you might know this title more for emma stone's oscar-winning 2023 adaptation, but the original poor things is just as quirky, subversive, and unforgettable — it's also rather different. D. Like the movie, Poor Things: Episodes from the Early Life of Archibald McCandless M. , Scottish Public Health Officer is a spin on Frankenstein focusing on Bella Baxter, a woman brought back to life with the brain of a baby in Victorian Glasgow.

Sebagaimana diketahui, like the movie, the book is wholly original, tracking bella's growth from an inexperienced, childlike girl into a liberated and knowledgeable young woman who learns, through experience, how to relate to and challenge the world's conventions. Gray's interest is entirely in offering a daring, postmodern dissection of Victorian society, particularly taking issue with the time's outdated social and sexual conventions. Most brilliant is the film's ending, in which letters from Bella herself put into question McCandless' retelling of her life, claiming she is neither the result of an experiment nor the idealized version that he depicts. It's one final, brilliant subversion of a well-known story that completely recontextualizes everything you just read.

Diungkapkan bahwa now we move on to one of the most critically acclaimed sci-fi books of the 2000s. A woman named Abigail Gentin has split herself into thousands of male and female clones known as shatterlings. House of Suns is set six million years into the future, as humanity has spread across the Milky Way. Two of them fall in love and arrive late to a family reunion, only to discover their fellow clones have been attacked by a mysterious force set on eradicating them.

Berdasarkan laporan, house of suns is among the most original, daring, and impactful explorations of identity in modern fiction. The result is one of the best sci-fi books of the 21st century, a remarkable and profound exercise in sci-fi that asks many intriguing questions without ever forgetting to deliver a compelling mystery. The premise is incredibly creative from the get-go, but the book's greatest strength is how it tackles issues of individuality within the context of a sprawling galaxy. How does one life matter in the grand context of the universe? Author Alastair Reynolds shoots for the stars here (pun intended). It's a bit under 500 pages, so you can comfortably end this one by Friday if you begin on Saturday morning.

Diungkapkan bahwa lastly, let's finish with one of the most popular and beloved sci-fi books of the 2010s. Andy Weir's best-selling juggernaut The Martian tells the story of Mark Watney, a botanist and engineer who becomes stranded on Mars after he's presumed dead. Left alone, and with only his wit and experience as allies, Watney has to, in his words, "science the s—t out of this. " Meanwhile, his crew on Earth works tirelessly to bring him home.

Berdasarkan laporan, weir creates genuine literary magic here. Watney's journey could become incredibly didactic, especially as he invests considerable time in his scientific process, using actual protocols and terms to survive. Yet, the author injects so much wit and personality into the writing that it practically comes alive before you. Watney is one of the best protagonists of the 21st century: ingenious, relatable, and remarkably human, endlessly optimistic despite being in a situation where so many others would've surrendered to despondency. It's no surprise that the book has become a true pop culture landmark, reviving mainstream interest in science fiction and launching Weir's career as one of the genre's best writers today.

#397. 3-Year-Old Told Babysitter 'Mama Cut Papa' After Mom Allegedly Killed BF

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.usmagazine.com/crime-news/news/florida-mom-charged-with-murder-after-girl-tells-babysitter/

A babysitter had been watching a Florida woman’s two children when the mother’s 3-year-old daughter started crying and said, “Mama cut papa,” court documents state.

The girl’s statement came the same day Orlando police discovered a man’s body in a trash bag between a dumpster and a trash compactor at the Pacifico Apartments in the city on Tuesday, November 9, according to court documents.

The child’s mother, Isidra Bautista Hernandez, is accused of killing her boyfriend inside their shared apartment at the complex two days earlier, on Saturday, November 7, and disposing of his body.

Hernandez, 36, was arrested on a second-degree murder charge in connection with the man’s death on Wednesday, November 11, Us previously reported.

An arrest affidavit obtained by Us reveals more details about the man’s killing, identifying him as Eugenio Martinez.

On Monday, two maintenance workers initially found a heavy black garbage bag “covered in flies” with what they suspected were human remains inside near the dumpster area of the Pacifico Apartments, resulting in a 911 call, according to the affidavit.

Orlando police arrived and initially saw a man’s arm, which was wrapped in a blue sheet, inside the bag, the affidavit states.

The man identified as Martinez, 32, “was tied with an orange extension cord and wrapped in 3 black trash bags and a dark blue laundry bag,” an officer wrote in the affidavit.

An autopsy revealed he had “laceration to his neck as well as puncture wounds on his left side, lacerations on his left palm, and lacerations on the left side of his face,” the affidavit states.

Detectives searched the trash compactor that was near Martinez’s body and found several items with suspected blood, including a black sandal, a piece of mail, a broken knife, towels and blankets, according to police.

The investigation led officers to execute a search warrant at Hernandez’s apartment, where suspected blood was found throughout the residence, which appeared to have been recently cleaned, the affidavit states.

While there, a 21-year-old woman approached detectives and revealed her mother had been babysitting Hernandez’s two children — a 3-year-old daughter and a 1-year-old son — since Saturday, when the alleged killing occurred.

She said on Monday, the girl cried out saying, “‘Mama cut papa’ and made hand gestures mimicking a slicing motion along her arms, stomach, and neck,” the affidavit states.

Hernandez’s daughter also mentioned “blood” and “trash” to the babysitter, according to the filing.

Diungkapkan bahwa hernandez, who had bruising on her arm, was detained and told officers she had been involved in a physical altercation with martinez, whom she described as her husband but noted they’re not legally married, on saturday, the affidavit states. She accused him of choking her while holding a long knife.

At some point, she said she took the knife from him and demonstrated a “slashing motion,” according to the filing.

“Hernandez advised that she did not contact law enforcement due to fear; however, she later placed two calls to 911 in hopes that someone would find the decedent at the dumpster,” the affidavit states.

She allegedly also admitted to placing Martinez’s body in trash bags and leaving it near the dumpster.

“Statements made by the couple’s young child referencing her mother cutting someone, along with the subsequent bruising on Hernandez’s arm, provide additional context surrounding the events preceding the decedent’s death,” the officer wrote in the affidavit.

Hernandez’s public defender didn’t immediately return a request for comment from Us on Friday, November 13.

Hernandez is due in court for a hearing set for November 17, records show.

Diungkapkan bahwa fortunately, i had the chance to ask leitch about how he pulled this off in "how to rob a bank" during a recent press junket. For Leitch, it was a matter of delineating between both aspects of writer Mark Bianculli's script and having form follow function:.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "there were two very different visual stories we were telling. Then you had these bombastic episodes of this charismatic content creator. Actually, the challenge opportunity was exciting to bring them together. We were telling the grounded story of these characters and their very relatable plights that are happening, that are a snapshot of our times. And we shot that on 35 millimeter and there was a very traditional visual style we chose intentionally for that. And then the challenge was bringing those two worlds together. ".

In fact, Leitch pinpoints the moment where these worlds finally collide.

Diungkapkan bahwa as much as "how to rob a bank" presents itself as a rollicking, thrill-a-minute roller coaster ride, things take an abrupt turn an hour in. Reilly's FBI Agent John West) track down their identities, and they soon land on opposite sides of an interrogation room. Our gang of bank-robbing Robin Hoods make a key mistake, their dogged pursuers (led by Zoë Kravitz's tech-wiz Reagan and John C. But, as the leader of this pack, Ryan has never found a setback he can't turn into a teachable moment — or, more cynically, a piece of content.

Diungkapkan bahwa that's exactly what happens here, when both halves of the movie come into focus. "I think where we do it really well, and it's my favorite scene in the movie," David Leitch explains to me, "is during the interrogation sequence, where we're blurring the lines between the Wolf's show — basically [explaining] how to survive an interrogation — and the actual footage, being in the real interrogation. " Here, Leitch and his creative team splice together straightforward imagery from the interrogation (which is mostly our defiant characters sitting silently, demanding their lawyer) and imagery where Ryan uses (or imagines?) this as his latest YouTube video: How to Survive an Interrogation.

According to Leitch, this allowed him to play with what we're seeing versus what's really happening:.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "even the characters in the movie breaking the fourth wall or texts coming up on the screen when we're in the film, now it's like [the] content creator visual style is changing the way that i'm telling you the narrative aspect of the film. And I'm actually using the narrative aspect of the film to influence the way that I composed the content creator footage. ".

Diungkapkan bahwa despite the complexity in putting this sequence together, all of this is seamlessly cut and presented in a way where it hardly even registers to moviegoers. At the moment, we're too concerned with the fate of Ryan, his lover Emi (Anna Sawai), and the rest of their friends as all their best-laid plans come crashing down. Adding to the tension is the delicate balance of power suddenly shifting away from these honorable thieves trying to make a societal point and towards the man representing all the structural ills they're fighting against: FBI Agent John West.

Diungkapkan bahwa during our conversation, "how to rob a bank" producer and 87north production company founder kelly mccormick chimes in and adds, "that's exactly where the power is shifting and where the worlds are colliding. " Intriguingly, none of this is meant to register to viewers who are (hopefully) absorbed by the storytelling in the moment. So, in a masterful way, [David Leitch is] toying with you there, manipulating you with both ways of storytelling. According to Leitch, this is something that he only conveyed through the subtext and through the visuals in how he and director of photography Jonathan Sela shot the scene:.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "it's not necessary for the audience to really understand it, but that's the uneasy feeling i'm trying to give, is the power switching. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, we won't give away anything that happens next, but it's safe to say this is the turning point where things kick into another gear. From that point on, the film's stakes are firmly set and nobody feels safe. "How to Rob a Bank" is now playing in theaters.

The rights to the "Friday the 13th" series have been stuck in a bit of a legal mess over the years, but according to an official press release from Horror, Inc. Steve Miner, who directed "Friday the 13th Part 2" and "Friday the 13th Part III" (which was the first movie to give Jason his now-iconic hockey mask) will direct this new entry.

Sebagaimana diketahui, some fans will no doubt love that jason is back on the big screen in any form, while more cynical folks (like me, for instance) will wonder if this is little more than an attempt to cling onto the complicated rights to a well-established franchise. Then again, it's not like these movies need to be complicated. We just want to see Jason hack and slash. In any case, the new "Friday the 13th" comes on the heels of "Crystal Lake," the TV series that served as an origin story for Jason and his killer mother.

Diungkapkan bahwa per the press release, horror, inc. Per Fleigel's IMDb page, this will apparently be his first produced screenplay. His only other credits are for producing and "additional crew. , under the leadership of the Barsamian family, will finance and produce the film, with CatchLight Studios as a production partner, and Cineverse securing North America distribution rights. David Fliegel will pen the script. ".

Berdasarkan laporan, the last time jason was up on the big screen was in 2009's "friday the 13th" reboot, which was a box office hit but did not spawn a whole new franchise as intended. Since then, the series has languished in a legal quagmire, with Jason only returning in a short film (titled "Sweet Revenge") and the aforementioned "Crystal Lake" series.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, as a kid who grew up haunting the horror section of the video store, i'm always up for some new jason action, and it does seem crazy that we haven't had a new "friday the 13th" movie in so long. I'm pulling for him.

#407. 6 Thriller Miniseries That Are 10/10, No Notes

📅 13 Nov 2026

6 Thriller Miniseries That Are 10/10, No Notes

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://collider.com/thriller-miniseries-perfect-no-notes/

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, with its unique ability to let a story unfold over the course of multiple hours while still delivering a succinct resolution that viewers don’t have to wait over the course of multiple seasons to see, the miniseries format has emerged as an outstanding forum for thriller entertainment. Even more impressive is that there has been no shortage of approaches that have worked within the parameters of limited series releases, with everything from action-packed bombast to simmering slow-burn anxiety and even piercing psychological horror having an impact.

Sebagaimana diketahui, these six series stand as true masterpieces of the genre in the format, with everything from murder mystery suspense to puncturing historical tension. Some of these series are universally heralded as being defining masterpieces of limited series drama and television entertainment at large, while others are criminally underrated gems that have never found the recognition and respect they so thoroughly deserve. All of them are faultless forays into small-screen thrills that all lovers of the genre must seek out if they haven’t seen them already.

Berdasarkan laporan, a bold recreation of david cronenberg’s 1988 movie of the same name, dead ringers is a visceral descent into psychologically twisting dread that grounds its heart-stopping suspense in its arresting visuals and rachel weisz’s captivating dual performance. She stars as Beverly and Elliot Mantle, twin sisters who share everything from their career path to lovers, drugs, and a frightful determination to bring their aspirations to life. As they perform ethically questionable procedures on infertile women in preparation for them opening their own independent birthing center, a rift begins to form between the two sisters when Beverly enters into a serious relationship with one of her clients, the famous actress Genevieve Cotard (Britne Oldford).

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the amazon prime series is certainly not for the faint of heart, and there have been viewers who voiced their displeasure with its graphic body horror, intentionally unlikable characters, and its abundant, vulgar profanity. However, if audiences can overcome the shocking content and grasp that it is intended to run as a thematically piercing and unrelenting exploration of co-dependency, identity, women’s healthcare, and the power amoral ambition can have when backed by immense wealth, Dead Ringers becomes an intriguing, albeit cold-hearted, viewing experience. Furthermore, it is one of the most fiendishly unsettling miniseries television has seen in many years, making it a must-see gem for genre enthusiasts.

Berdasarkan laporan, a bbc production from the early 2000s that has sadly been completely forgotten over time, state of play is an engrossing mixture of political conspiracy thrills, murder mystery intrigue, and newsroom drama. While investigating the gang-related killing of a teenager, reporter Cal McCaffrey (John Simm) and his colleagues discover a link between the crime and the death of a young political researcher for rising MP, Stephen Collins (David Morrissey). As the newspaper’s investigation pries deeper, they uncover not only the connection of the murders, but a scandalous love affair as well as a conspiracy tying high-ranking British government figures to corruption in the petroleum industry.

Sebagaimana diketahui, written and created by paul abbott and directed by david yates, state of play finds its suspense in its grit and realism. It embeds viewers in the raw, confronting truths of the institutions it explores, from the greed and ambition of political parties to the amoral, story-driven sensationalism of news media. This striking sense of ambiguous righteousness and authentic dread is only heightened by the incredible ensemble cast that includes Bill Nighy, James McAvoy, and Kelly Macdonald, the patient yet propulsive six-hour progression of the story, and the razor-sharp nature of the character dynamics and dialogue.

Sebagaimana diketahui, an excellent blending of mystery, suspense, and sci-fi intrigue, devs is one of the best miniseries of the 2020s so far. Unfortunately, its hostile tone of suspicion and corporate cynicism was a far cry from what audiences were craving at the height of the COVID-19 pandemic, and it has since faded from memory. However, the FX/Hulu release is well worth revisiting, with the eight-part miniseries revolving around the mysterious and shocking death of a newly promoted employee, and the endeavor of Lily Chan (Sonoya Mizuno)—the deceased’s colleague and romantic partner—to figure out the truth behind Amaya and its enigmatic CEO, Forest (Nick Offerman).

Diungkapkan bahwa written, directed, and created by alex garland, devs combines its patient and meticulous pacing with an overwhelming sense of thematic gravitas. Lily’s investigation doesn’t just examine the nature of corporate secrecy and professional malpractice; it revels in the depths of such ideas as determinism and free will, theories of multiverses and alternate realities, and the piercing influence of grief and the search for absolution. Complimented by astonishing production design, a uniquely haunting soundscape comprised of expressionistic quantum computer sounds and its eerie score, and the layered complexity of the performances, Devs stands as a sorely overlooked thriller that blends techno-thriller boldness with philosophical depth and mystery suspense to perfection.

Diungkapkan bahwa using the murder mystery format as a platform for piercing character drama and introspective thematic journeys rather than simply as a tightly-paced whodunit thriller, sharp objects stands as one of the more psychologically impressionable miniseries in recent years. Based on Gillian Flynn’s novel, it follows crime reporter Camille Preaker (Amy Adams) as she returns to her hometown of Wind Gap, Missouri, to investigate the murders of two young girls. As she investigates the disturbing case, she must also navigate the re-emerging traumas of her youth, many of which pertain to her strained relationship with her cruel, socialite mother and her shy half-sister.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the underappreciated hbo miniseries benefits greatly from jean-marc vallée’s direction in all eight episodes, with the consistent vision allowing for the story to unfurl with a methodical majesty against a backdrop of small-town malevolence and eerie southern gothic atmosphere. Even as it flicks between Camille’s investigation and her troubled youth, juxtaposing an adult’s jaded world-weariness against young Camille’s (Sophia Lillis) arduous existence under her domineering mother, Sharp Objects maintains a patient though propulsive drive, one defined by a litany of shocking plot twists and outstanding performances from all involved.

Berdasarkan laporan, most miniseries that excel do so by mastering one form of storytelling. It initially runs as a framed innocent man thriller with murder mystery inflections, following Pakistani-American youth Nasir (Riz Ahmed) as he awakens after a night of partying to find his date has been stabbed to death. The Night Of effectively perfects four different subgenres of crime suspense throughout its eight-episode run. As he stands trial and awaits prosecution, the series incorporates courtroom thrills and prison yard tension into the fold, while dogged defense attorney John Stone’s (John Turturro) story mixes investigative lawyer case work with a certain social commentary about wealth and corporate power.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the miniseries as a whole runs as a transfixing crime thriller that asks demanding questions about the integrity and fairness of america’s legal system. This rousing thematic focus is brilliantly supported by exceptional performances and stunning cinematic visuals that exude a sense of simmering, slow-burning intensity. The novelistic ambition of The Night Of as both a character-focused drama and a skewering critique of criminal justice institutions is remarkable, making for a flawless masterpiece of crime thriller television that, even 10 years on from its release, remains an underrated gem from HBO.

Berdasarkan laporan, it may not immediately spring to mind when one thinks of television thrillers—after all, it is defined as being a historical drama—but it is difficult to name a more relentlessly intense and agonizingly suspenseful miniseries than chernobyl. A defining masterpiece of HBO’s production prowess, it explores the aftermath of the Chernobyl nuclear power plant disaster of 1986, covering the horrific experiences of the unsuspecting first responders, the enormity of the operation to contain the radioactive fallout, and the scheming of the Soviet leaders to conceal the true scale of the catastrophe from the world.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the series excels as a commentary on political corruption, an ode to the heroes who sacrificed their lives to restrict the fallout, and an eye-opening cautionary tale of the dangers of nuclear power, but chernobyl is best remembered by many for its ferocious sense of tension. Much of it comes because the audiences know the devastating scope of the reactor meltdown, whereas the characters are examining it as it happens, an approach that makes the inescapable threat of radiation poisoning feel like a damning certainty, a stalking, invisible monster. The ticking clock of objectives that must be completed only heightens this sense of fatalistic dread, especially as the desperate stakes are only interrupted by the folly of bureaucratic process. Great performances and rousing thematic sharpness are the icing on the cake, consolidating Chernobyl as the most gripping and grueling television thriller of all time, miniseries or otherwise.

S. , "Steel Magnolias" keeps the story isolated to a group of women played by Sally Field, Shirley MacLaine, Daryl Hannah, Olympia Dukakis, Julia Roberts, and the late Dolly Parton. Directed by Herbert Ross and written by Robert Harling, based on his own 1987 stage play of the same name, the film is both tragic and funny as we follow the ups, downs, and in-betweens of these charming and occasionally sassy ladies.

The script [. ] is on a degenerated line from Tennessee Williams by way of Hallmark cards. ".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the laughter and the tears are exactly why we're talking about "steel magnolias" now, as it's full of delightful quips and barbs alongside sentiments that might feel like greeting card schmaltz but still pack charm and an emotional punch. Diungkapkan bahwa one of the driving forces of "steel magnolias" is julia roberts as shelby eatenton-latcherie, a role for which she earned an academy award nomination for best supporting actress. Shelby has type 1 diabetes, which turns her hope for having children into a health risk. Sadly, as Shelby pursues her motherly desire, the pregnancy damages her kidneys, and she's forced to go on dialysis. But Shelby's mother, Mary Lynn "M'Lynn" Eatenton (Sally Field) is able to donate a kidney to help save her from further grief.

Sebagaimana diketahui, unfortunately, shelby dies due to an infection caused by the suppressive therapy that keeps her body from rejecting the kidney. Stuck unconscious in a hospital, Shelby's family makes the difficult decision to take her off life support.

Diungkapkan bahwa after the funeral, m'lynn is overwhelmed. In a burst of emotion, she swings dramatically through pain, anger, sadness, and disbelief, but then there's a bit of laughter. M'Lynn expresses that she "just wants to hit somebody" until they feel as bad as she does. That's when M'Lynn's friend Clairee Belcher (Olympia Dukakis) offers up Louisa "Ouiser" Boudreaux (Shirley Maclaine) for M'Lynn to punch, much to Ouiser's disbelief and the shock of the other women. It's a hilarious moment that eases the tension and offers some relief.

In the aftermath, M'Lynn apologizes for her emotional outburst, but Truvy offers consolation by saying:.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "laughter through tears is my favorite emotion. ".

Berdasarkan laporan, you can see the hallmark-tinged vibe of a line like that, but being cheesy doesn't make it any less true. You don't have to laugh to keep from crying. In the shadow of tragedy, laughing through tears offers a welcome break from the exhaustion of grief. After the death of a loved one, you may even find yourself making dark jokes to cope with the sadness and anger that you feel, and that's okay. Instead, you can laugh through the tears.

Here are some other memorable quotes from "Steel Magnolias," each with its own charm:.

Diungkapkan bahwa "smile! it increases your face value. " — Truvy Jones.

"Well, you know what they say: if you don't have anything nice to say about anybody, come sit by me!" — Clairee Belcher.

"I'm not crazy, I've just been in a very bad mood 40 years!" — Ouiser Boudreaux.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "honey, time marches on, and eventually, you realize it is marchin' across your face. " — Truvy Jones.

Berdasarkan laporan, "the only thing that separates us from the animals is our ability to accessorize. " — Clairee Belcher.

Berdasarkan laporan, "i would rather have 30 minutes of wonderful than a lifetime of nothing special. " — Shelby Eatenton-Latcherie.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "a dirty mind is a terrible thing to waste. " — Ouiser Boudreaux.

Berdasarkan laporan, "i have a strict policy that nobody cries alone in my presence. " — Truvy Jones.

#413. Cities: Skylines' Best Replacement Is Finally Here and Better than Expected

📅 13 Nov 2026

Cities: Skylines' Best Replacement Is Finally Here and Better than Expected

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.polygon.com/transport-fever-3-logistics-city-builder-game/

Transport Fever 3 turned me into a logistics nerd.

Transport Fever 3 turned me into a logistics nerd.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, 2026 is the year i got massively into city builders, and by massively i mean i played cities: skylines more than anything else for the first half of the year. I started dabbling with city builder-slash-logistics games in the second half of the year, like Anno 117, and turned my attention to Transport Fever 3 soon after. When I first learned about Transport Fever 3, I called it "like" Cities: Skylines. It looked a lot like a traditional city builder, albeit one where you focus on roads more than zoning. After playing it over the last month or so, though, I realize the difference between city builder and logistics planner is a lot more distinct than I initially gave it credit for — and I've irreversibly become a logistics sicko.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the first thing you do in cities: skylines is build a road, and then you start earmarking plots of land for residential and commercial zoning. It's a design and aesthetics challenge more than anything, though. The biggest logistics puzzles you end up solving involve road improvements, or more accurately, managing traffic as your city gets bigger. In the struggle to make roads big enough to handle the needs of a growing city, keeping things from looking like a dystopian hellscape is more important than optimizing traffic flow. Well, for me it is anyway, but the game's comparatively lax management requirements let personal preference prevail over logistical needs.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, not so with transport fever 3. Most resource nodes exist on map tiles outside your main metro area anyway, so you can just position any old road how you’d like and go on about your business. Once you have the money, you just construct the necessary buildings as close to the resource as possible and make sure there's a road that can link them back to the main city for deliveries. This small-but-important difference captured me instantly. Planning industries in Cities usually takes little foresight. Then you encourage new industry by making more lines that connect resource deposits with processing facilities in, or near, the town. The first task is creating a small network of transport lines to support consumer travel and industrial growth. Here, you start with a small town and a burgeoning transport company. Or you can just ignore industry entirely and turn your town into a strip mall paradise.

Sebagaimana diketahui, but the goal in transport fever 3 is to grow the existing town, and it won't grow without industry. Country roads aren't suitable for all types of travel, though, so you have to find alternative solutions to ensure the people living there have access to all the goods and transportation methods they need. You find places suitable for residential building and industry like in Cities, but it all builds up based on roads and road types, which gives you more control over how everything develops and more challenges to solve. Opting for a country road influences the kind of residential areas that will populate along it and makes it easier to create neighborhood-like areas, for example, as opposed to having homes just pop up inconveniently on a standard road. More people need more food, more places to work, and more ways to get to work, ideally on time and without being crammed on a tiny coach ill-adapted for the purpose. Multiply those considerations for every new residential and commercial area, imagine designing a functional and aesthetically pleasing infrastructure network to accommodate them, and you've got an idea of how this game works.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, there are a slew of other considerations to deal with, too. Terrain gradient determines the type of road you need — and now much it'll cost to maintain — so freight vehicles don't get stuck. That's true for pretty much every transport improvement. Trains are wonderful for moving goods and people, but require special production chains in place to operate, which puts another burden on your local infrastructure. It makes one area easier, but requires a lot more planning and work to keep others from spiraling out of control.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, it's all comparatively easy to maintain when settlements are smaller, and in sandbox mode, the game doesn't punish you for keeping things small. As long as your business isn't bankrupt, you're winning. Heck, you can have a bunch of mid-sized towns connected via water transport and airports if you want. But once your town grows into a city with multiple districts, managing everything is a nested stack of challenges that just gets more complex as time passes.

Berdasarkan laporan, a weekly cheat sheet to what you’ll eventually love to play. No buying, no commitment — just saving for later.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, which, it turns out, is exactly what i want. Make a new district, zone it like the last one — or, how about this for excitement, get a bit wild and invert the zoning swatches — connect the roads, add more power and water, proceed like before. I frequently find myself speeding up the simulation in Cities until some disaster or other requires my direct intervention. It's very passive once you get to a certain point, where improvements are additive and routine. That hands-off feeling never disappears in Transport Fever 3. I certainly still enjoy designing a huge city and seeing the results of my planning pay off, but I miss the hands-on requirements of early city building. It's a never-ending puzzle that captured me and won't let me go, and I couldn't be happier about it.

Combolands: Roguelike Citybuilder has one heck of a foundation.

Berdasarkan laporan, it’s a big weekend for new tv. VisionQuest has concluded its first season, including a post-credits scene with big implications for Avengers: Doomsday. The Lord of the Rings: Rings of Power is back with a third season, continuing the story of a Middle-earth set thousands of years before Bilbo and Frodo Baggins. The Body is also available on Netflix, delivering a fun and campy high school drama with some religious horror thrown in the mix.

Sebagaimana diketahui, thriller lovers have some shows to look forward to. It’s adapted by Slaughter herself, making her the rare novelist who’s also the showrunner for her own story. The Good Daughter, a 6-episode series based on Karin Slaughter's bestseller, has just been released. There’s also 12 12 12, starring Anthony Mackie and Jamie Dornan, as two men involved in a high-stakes cat-and-mouse game that starts with a robbery.

Berdasarkan laporan, we have a few picks for lovers of documentary and true crime. Murder in Galicia is streaming on Netflix, telling the story of the murder of 66-year-old Isabel Fuente, who was beaten in her sleep, with her husband claiming that some intruders had gotten inside their house.

Sebagaimana diketahui, there’s also hbo’s silent night, a series based on the murders that took place on christmas eve in 1976 in a small community in poland. Lastly, if you want something a little breezier, there’s The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives: Orange County, premiering on Hulu and Disney. Happy watching!.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the lord of the rings: rings of power is back with a third season, exploring the tales of middle-earth thousands of years before the events of the hobbit and the lord of the rings. Season 3 tries to course-correct a series that has never managed to get things right. Set five years after the events of season 2 and billed as a soft reboot to welcome in new watchers, the season finds Sauron establishing his power.

Diungkapkan bahwa prequels always have difficulty justifying their existence since it’s a foregone conclusion how the story will end. Last season, Rings of Power leaned into that inevitability in the same way as the Game of Thrones prequel House of the Dragon, building a Shakespearean tragedy from the corruption of the dwarf king Durin III (Peter Mullan) and the elven smith Celebrimbor (Charles Edwards). There’s still some of that in season 3 as the island kingdom of Númenor and the dwarven stronghold of Khazad-dûm inch closer to their dark fates. But the show also spends too much time taking the same approach as Solo: A Star Wars Story, providing unnecessary origins for everything from the construction plans of Lothlorien to the origins Gandalf’s hat.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the body is set in 2004 and follows a dance team at a catholic high school located somewhere in the northeast. After partying too hard and botching a dance initiation ceremony, the girls inspire a mass hysteria in the town, with residents believing they have a saint in their midst.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, one of the best parts of the body is its many references. The show’s cast of characters take these archetypes and complicate them. With dyed eyebrows and a sweet but alienating approach, Lisbeth feels like Needy from Jennifer’s Body with a dash of Brigitte from Ginger Snaps. Shephard borrows archetypes and textures from films like Bring It On, Mean Girls, and White Chicks. Anya and Elise are clear successors to Bring It On’s Torrance and Missy, who raised a generation of queer viewers with their ridiculously charged friendship. Story-wise, there are clear shades of The Crucible and The Exorcist. But the great thing about The Body is that even though it depicts the aughts and the social concerns of the era, it’s made in 2026, allowing the writers to revisit these tropes and probe further.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, set in georgia, the good daughter follows two estranged sisters reunited by a school shooting that may be closely tied to their past. The women have spent years apart due to an incident in their childhoods, when a group of men broke into their home, killing their mother and leaving one of them gravely injured.

Following a massive heist in Europe, 12 12 12 follows three timelines and two main characters: Paul (Jamie Dornan), the skilled criminal who pulled off the heist, and Jack (Anthony Mackie), a disgraced FBI agent with a personal vendetta against Paul.

Sebagaimana diketahui, based on the real-life crime of isabel fuente, “murder in galicia” is a scripted series following a seemingly perfect aging couple based in a small town in spain. After the woman is almost beaten to death after a break-in at their house, a civil guard becomes convinced that the culprit is actually the husband.

Based on a series of notorious crimes that took place on Christmas Eve in a small town in ‘70s Poland, the 6-episode series tells the story of the three murders that were committed on a snowy night in the town, initially staged as a hit-and-run.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the spin-off series trades the internet-famous salt lake city moms and swaps them for a new location: orange county. The new reality series follows a new batch of influencers and features moments captured in famous reality TV destinations like Laguna Beach and Huntington Beach.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, power, the starz series that ran for six seasons, is now available on netflix in full. The show follows a wealthy New York City club owner who’s also a drug kingpin and is trying to leave his life of crime behind to protect and focus on his family.

Diungkapkan bahwa i was most of the way through a full friends rewatch when the doc-series the one about matthew perry debuted for those with a netflix subscription, and i was on the fence about watching it. I wasn't sure I was up for a deeper dive into the actor's substance abuse struggles amidst conjuring fond memories of one of my favorite series. Friends is one of my comfort shows, and I knew this new docuseries was going to have the opposite effect, as it'd be a heartbreaking reminder of the tragic ending that befell Perry in 2023 -- his death was ultimately ruled an accident, with ketamine use among the contributing factors.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, still, i felt compelled to watch the netflix docuseries, and yes, it was uncomfortable and sad and a lot of other things, but there's one thing that really hit me hard about the story that's told across three episodes, and that's just how hard matthew perry struggled with his addiction. When I say struggled, I don't just mean that the docuseries focused heavily on his substance abuse, I mean that it emphasized and helped me understand how he battled with that addiction for years.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i admit, i didn't follow the actor's personal life particularly closely in the years during or after friends aired. It was still public knowledge that Perry had trouble with addiction over the years, and that he'd been to rehab. What The One About Matthew Perry really made clear to me, through the use of interviews from his sister (Mia Perry Bowick) and other people who knew him at some point in his life, was how hard he tried to get and stay sober in the decades before he died, including a lot of time and money spent on rehabilitation treatment.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, from the accounts of friends and loved ones, we learn more about his trips to rehab and efforts to stay clean afterward, while also building a career for himself as an entertainer. It's a fascinating look at the different dimensions of the comedic actor, and I very much appreciated that the goal seemed to be to help viewers understand him better (as opposed to making a spectacle of his life).

Diungkapkan bahwa my understanding of drug addiction and alcoholism is admittedly pretty limited. But the struggle many go through over years or even decades to get and stay clean is something I want to understand better. A lot of what I know about the most extreme cases comes from the media (news, movies/TV shows), which I think is a big reason why my perception of it probably isn't very balanced. So much of the focus of substance abuse, as I've seen it, is on the harm it causes -- for the person and the people around them -- and that's important. Maybe I'll never fully understand how difficult sobriety is, having not struggled with addiction myself, but I want to understand it as best I can.

Berdasarkan laporan, matthew perry's experience trying repeatedly to get his addiction in check and his life and career on track is illustrated vividly in the one with matthew perry. There's more to the docuseries -- including some humor, the relationships he had with friends and family, his time on Friends, and his goals within his career and as a person -- but the growth he was trying to achieve over the years is really what struck me most. It left me wanting to read (or listen to) his memoir, so I can learn even more about what he went through, this time from his own perspective.

Sebagaimana diketahui, kelly put her life-long love of movies, tv and books to greater use when she joined cinemablend as a freelance tv news writer in 2006, and went on to serve as the site’s tv editor before joining the staff full-time in 2011 and moving over to other roles at the site. At present, she’s an Assistant Managing Editor who spends much of her time brainstorming and editing features, analyzing site data, working with writers and editors on content planning and the workflow, and obsessing over the best movies and TV shows. She graduated from SUNY Cortland with BA in Communication Studies and a minor in Cinema Studies. When she isn't working, she's probably thinking about work, or reading (or listening to a book), and making sure her cats are living their absolute best feline lives.

Diungkapkan bahwa it's been a wild week for fans of the superhero genre. While VisionQuest's finale teased the return of a beloved Marvel hero, moviegoers are still recovering from the change of leadership happening at DC. Between James Gunn being removed as co-CEO of DC Studios and Henry Cavill talking about Superman, fans are feeling a bit frazzled. Although I have another hot take about the ongoing situation.

Diungkapkan bahwa back in 2022, james gunn and peter safran were announced at ceos of dc studios, and over the past four years they crafted a new shared universe for theaters (and streaming with a hbo max subscription). While the DCU is still in its infancy, fans are curious about whether the original plan for the first slate of projects, titled Gods and Monsters are still happening. Let's break down the situation, as well as my hot take about Superman.

Berdasarkan laporan, earlier this week news broke that both james gunn and peter safran were stepping down from their role as co-ceos of dc studios. The pair will be replaced by Former Marvel Studios executive Jeremy Latcham, who worked on projects like Iron Man, the first two Avengers movies, and Spider-Man: Homecoming. The news came as a shock, especially so shortly after Clayface hit theaters.

Sebagaimana diketahui, by all accounts it looks like gunn was fired, but he offered some silver lining when issuing a statement on his instagram. Part of that statement reads:.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, but what only the closest people to me have known over the past four years is my time at dc studios has been trying, to say the last. I dislike the at-times corporate nature of the job (thanks to Peter for taking the brunt of that. ) I'm always a very hard worker, but as a filmmaker I would at least get to short breaks to unwind, and I've stolen even that time from both myself and my loved ones over the past four years.

Sebagaimana diketahui, while gunn will stop serving as the head of dc on december 1st, he's still got some involvement in the shared universe. He's the director of Man of Tomorrow, which wrapped principal photography back in August. He's also a producer on The Batman: Part Two, which is expected to hit theaters in 2028.

Berdasarkan laporan, there are countless questions about what'll come next for the dcu, especially since its so early into its life on the screen. The 43 year-old actor recently spoke to Inverse and was asked if he'd play the Man of Steel again. A. ”.

The Bachelor has officially chosen a new lead to hand out roses on season 30.

Sebagaimana diketahui, nfl quarterback sam hartman was announced as the season 30 bachelor on friday, november 13, joining good morning america with a football in hand. The 27-year-old opened up about how he got involved in the reality dating show, admitting he had some hesitation at first.

Berdasarkan laporan, “honestly, at first i was like, ‘no way,'” he said. “I got really lucky and talked to Jesse Palmer and he kind of gave me the insight, what it is and what it’s not. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, despite his initial fears, hartman added that he couldn’t pass up the chance to find the love of his life. “I don’t see any problem with that. “When people are saying ‘I do,’ they don’t ask where you met, they just ask if you wanna do it forever,” he continued. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa when it comes to how he’ll approach dating multiple women at once, hartman said he’s “very nervous. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “i have a tough time having a conversation with one girl, [so] 30 is gonna be pretty tough,” he joked. “I’m excited but also very nervous. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, hartman’s family is also excited to see how his journey will play out. “My mom and I have a really cool relationship, my pops is just supportive,” he said. “Their big thing is just being myself and enjoy the experience. Trust your instincts and trust your gut. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa as for what he’s looking for in a partner, hartman said he likes “competitiveness” — but not necessarily in an athletic way. He explained that he’s a fan of the chase.

Diungkapkan bahwa “not chase in a way that you haven’t texted me back in a week, but chase in a way that they have a drive for something that motivates me to wake up every day and chase them,” hartman said. My whole family is in the medical field … seeing them do so much for other people, I think that’s a huge part. “Also a part of that is compassion and some type of caregiving. ”.

Hartman played college football for both the Wake Forest Demon Deacons and the Notre Dame Fighting Irish before signing with the Washington Commanders in 2024 as an undrafted free agent.

Diungkapkan bahwa his casting comes after abc pulled taylor frankie paul‘s season 22 of the bachelorette days before it was expected to premiere in march amid reports of a domestic violence incident involving her ex dakota mortensen. Candace Cameron Bure looked to her faith to keep her going on Special Forces: World’s Toughest Test season 5.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “i memorized a lot of scripture before i left,” candace, 50, exclusively told us ahead of the season 5 finale on thursday, november 12, during a joint interview with husband valeri bure. “Just memorizing scripture about fear and perseverance and endurance. There was a constant reel in my mind that I was just citing scripture, just giving myself the encouragement to walk through it. ”.

Candace shared that she and the other fellow recruits “had really great conversations” at night while spending time in their barrack, which was located in the jungles of Malaysia.

Diungkapkan bahwa “we were saying prayers at night,” she said. It had a huge impact on me, to keep me going. “There were other Christian believers in the room, so it was a source of comfort for me, but I think for a lot of us in the room. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, while on the show, candace climbed down a 30-foot rope ladder hanging off a suspension bridge, navigated the stomach flu and jumped out of a helicopter — just to name a few of her feats. But what pushed Candace close to her breaking point was the chemical warfare challenge featuring tear gas.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “i thought i was going to die. I was ready to leave the show at that point,” she admitted to Us, adding that she thought she was “genuinely gonna quit. ”.

In the heat of the moment, Candace took off her arm band — which typically signals a voluntary withdrawal from the recruit — but the footage didn’t air on TV.

Berdasarkan laporan, “what you didn’t see is that i actually did rip up my like rip off my armband because i thought i was trapped in the tear gas,” she told us. I ripped it out, like, ‘I need to get out. “I didn’t know that there was an exit and I thought I was about to die because it swells your neck, you’re burning, you’re itching, and I just wanted to get out. I need to get out. ’”.

Candace admitted that she “wasn’t rationally thinking” at the moment, noting that she “didn’t have to withdraw” just to leave the challenge.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “once i got out, i thought that was it for me,” she recalled. I was just so panicked and didn’t know how to get out. ’ And I put it back on, and I was actually relieved because I’m like I didn’t want to leave the show. “And one of the DS, [Jason “Foxy” Fox], he actually picked up my armband and goes, ‘I think you dropped this, didn’t you?’ And I was like, ‘Yes, yes, sir, yes, staff. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, candace, alongside collin gosselin and alexia umansky, ultimately passed selection in the season 5 finale. While recalling the moment, Candace admitted she felt “shocked” that she made it to the end.

Berdasarkan laporan, “that whole night — it was a 24-hour day, so you are so sleep deprived and you don’t know what’s going on. I didn’t know we were at the final selection,” she told Us. ’ And it was just fun to share it with the others too. ".

When Does The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping Hit Theaters?.

What Is The Hunger Games Book Sunrise on the Reaping About?.

Sebagaimana diketahui, this book is a prequel to the hunger games and takes place 24 years prior to when readers first met katniss everdeen. "This year, in honor of the Quarter Quell, twice as many tributes will be taken from their homes. "As the day dawns on the fiftieth annual Hunger Games, fear grips the districts of Panem," the description on author Suzanne Collins' website reads. #461. 5 Takeaways From China’s Golden Rooster and Hundred Flowers Film Festival

📅 14 Nov 2026

5 Takeaways From China’s Golden Rooster and Hundred Flowers Film Festival

Tanggal: 14 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/takeaways-china-golden-rooster-hundred-flowers-film-festival-1236755329/

Beyond Tony Leung Ka Fai’s win and a big night for local hits, a week of seminars and workshops showed how China’s industry is thinking about AI, global audiences and young talent.

China celebrated its Golden Rooster Awards this past Tuesday night in a glittering ceremony hosted inside the palatial Xiamen Strait Grand Theater in Xiamen, Fujian Province, China.

The southern seaside city hosted generations of stars — from current hotshot Jackson Yee (Resurrection) to acclaimed auteur Zhang Yimou — for an event that is the highlight of the annual state-run Golden Rooster and Hundred Flowers Film Festival.

Sebagaimana diketahui, hong kong’s tony leung ka fai stole the show, winning his first golden rooster best actor nod for his turn as the villain in the larry yang-directed thriller the shadow’s edge — some 25 years on from sending hearts a flutter across the globe in jean-jacques annaud’s steamy the lover. One Monk. Two Estranged Irish Brothers Facing Trauma. Related Stories Movies 'One Sweet Hour': One Aging Elvis Impersonator. Movies How 'Red Ink' Pulled Off a Single-Take, 1940s Vampire Newsroom Thriller.

“I hope this is just the beginning of new journey,” said the veteran of more than 140 movies.

Behind the scenes the business of making movies was very much front and center, as the Chinese industry gathered for seminars and workshops it hopes will chart its future course.

Here’s what The Hollywood Reporter learned from the week:.

Yimou Urges Filmmakers to Stay Focused on the Story.

Sebagaimana diketahui, zhang yimou brought a sense of gravitas to proceedings across the week. The 76-year-old was there among all the fanfare at the event’s Golden Rooster Awards, handing out the Best Feature Film award to director Shen Ao and his WW2 drama Dead to Rights while also mingling with all the stars and watching on — in awe, like everyone in the room — as a massive dragon drone cruised the air overhead.

Yimou had also helped launch the industry side of proceedings with a “Stories That Travel: Chinese and Asian Cinema in Dialogue with the World” seminar that gathered reps from international festivals and, soon enough, saw talk turn to Artificial Intelligence and its effect on cinema.

With Zhang’s adaptation of Liu Cixin sci-fi classic The Three-Body Problem in the works the director revealed he’d started to dabble in the tech, with a dedicated team set up on set to explore how AI could be adapted to the filmmaking process.

In his own inimitable way, the director then set the scene for the week ahead when he urged his fellow filmmakers to do the same — but to never lose site of the main ingredient: The story.

Berdasarkan laporan, “the new technology is moving too fast,” the director said. But for me filmmaking is about the story that’s in my heart, and the only thing I can do is to tell it the best way I can. “The moment you blink, you are behind it. So, embrace this era. ”.

Star-Studded Golden Roosters Celebrate a Big Year for the Locals.

The news coming into the week was that so far this year Chinese cinemas have been dominated by Chinese movies, with eight of the year’s box office top 10 being domestic productions.

The industry itself has been big on spreading a message of diversification of content, and to that end the two films that dominated “China’s Oscars” could not possibly be more different in either style nor in content.

Sebagaimana diketahui, shen’s dead to rights — with golden rooster best actress winner gao ye shining — collected more than $380 million and sets itself around the infamous nanjing massacre and the real-life story of the photo studio that documented the horror. It’s a gripping often brutal tale — and features two of China’s most bankable stars in Gao and Liu Haoran (Detective Chinatown).

Sebagaimana diketahui, lan hongchun’s dear you — winner of both special jury prize and best screenplay — collected around $300 million and sets itself around the story of one of the thousands of migrant chinese families separated through economic necessity in the 1950s and ’60s. It’s a languid tear-jerker, and it stars a cast of complete unknowns.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, dear you was the surprise hit of the year in china and it reached an enthusiastic global audience. Lan was beside himself on stage. “It feels like I’m dreaming,” he said. “I want to thank my grandma in heaven, because she told me so many stories when I was little. ”.

Opening night under the stars at the Bailuzhou Park Water Square in Xiamen was a treat for the young families who packed the venue for the China debut of another film that speaks to the Chinese diaspora and — the filmmakers hope — will to the domestic audience too.

Diungkapkan bahwa the singapore-spain-italy production the violinist has already won best film at the 2026 annecy international animation film festival and best animated film at the 19th asia pacific screen awards. Set among the Chinese community, it follows the fortunes of two childhood friends separated by war, and it had the audience, including all those kids, transfixed.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “singapore’s animation industry is very small, and the country is small too. “We started by looking overseas for co-producers. As it happened, we had a lot of friends in the animation industry. So, with a production of this scale, one person can’t do it alone,” co-director Ervin Han explained. So, all together, we’re telling a story about a part of the history of us Singaporean Chinese. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, producer cristiano bortone also took to the stage before the premiere and picked up on what was one of the central themes of this year’s festival: sharing chinese stories with the world. Bortone The Violinist “delves deeply into Chinese and Asian culture, while also capturing a European style and sensibility. ”.

“This is the beauty of blending our cultures,” he added.

China’s next generation was out in force across the industry events, and they basically filled the room at the “Golden Rooster Film Academy II: Ark Lab AI” workshop.

Diungkapkan bahwa lan tian, the creative director behind joint-generation ai model seedance 2. 5, took the room and didn’t shy away from exploring its impact in what turned into a candid discussion about how the technology was already impacting the film industry.

Berdasarkan laporan, the ai industry has been embraced in china arguably like anywhere else, and already has an estimated worth of around $176 billion, while the short-drama and digital film market is expected to top $6 billion this year. The pitch from Lan was on the savings the new tech can provide.

“If you get an investment of one million, or less than one million you might be able to produce something that looks like it cost 10 million,” he said.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, but lan’s push was also to use his technology as a tool that supports “reality. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “my girlfriend is an actor so i know there is concern,” he said. But I want this prop to be real, too. “The creative approach I’m talking about may only require a studio and some props that interact with the actors. For instance, if I need to drink water, I want the water to be real. ”.

Festival Spotlight Turns to Young Filmmakers.

While AI dominated proceedings, it was encouraging to see young filmmakers committed to the traditions of cinema out and about.

Diungkapkan bahwa yan siyu was among those featured during pitching sessions that placed emerging talent in front of international festival and studio reps. Her debut Outside The Room of My Own focusses on the journey three generation of women who take back to their ancestral village, and she echoed the words of Zhang that had opened the whole week.

Berdasarkan laporan, “i want to reach out to people to let them know there is this film in china. “This film is not just my work, because I have a lot of people supporting me. It’s a female director’s debut and I can say it’s a really good film,” she said. It’s a story that comes from my heart — and in telling it I am sharing my deepest feelings. I can’t let them down. ”.
