#466. In Canada: Canada Music Fund to Receive $67M Boost; Women in Music Executive Award Winners Share Their Wisdom

📅 14 Nov 2026

In Canada: Canada Music Fund to Receive $67M Boost; Women in Music Executive Award Winners Share Their Wisdom

Tanggal: 14 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.billboard.com/pro/canada-music-fund-67m-boost-canada-news/

Also this week: Sean Paul appears on the first episode of Billboard Canada News.

The Canada Music Fund is getting a new boost from the federal government.

Berdasarkan laporan, at last night’s adisq gala in montreal (nov. 8), the Minister of Canadian Identity and Culture, Marc Miller, announced that the federal government will invest $67 million to the Canada Music Fund, as part of the government’s promised $600 million investment into the cultural sector. The sum was first announced in June to provide “immediate relief” to the country’s audio and audiovisual sector and confirmed for 2026-27 in the latest federal budget, which was tabled last week. Over the weekend, Ottawa gave a long-awaited breakdown of how the funds will be allocated.

Diungkapkan bahwa the music sector will receive its share of the relief investment through the canada music fund, which was renewed through 2028 last year. The $67 million sum will be distributed to the five organizations that the fund supports, with FACTOR (Foundation Assisting Canadian Talent on Recordings) receiving $31. 7 million, the RadioStar fund receiving $3. 5 million, Musicaction (which funds and supports Francophone music and music companies) receiving $21 million, the Canadian Starmaker Fund receiving $5. 8 million and the Indigenous Music Office (IMO) receiving $5 million.

Diungkapkan bahwa last november, the imo released a new national report outlining ways in which the federal government could help indigenous artists and their music connect with bigger audiences, notably through increased discoverability on streaming platforms. Each of the funds will help support and foster emerging Canadian acts and help them compete on the world stage.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “canada’s cultural sovereignty depends on our willingness to invest in our own voices,” says meg symsyk, president and ceo of factor. Our responsibility is to give that talent the opportunity to be heard, to build lasting careers and to reach audiences here at home and around the world. “We have extraordinary talent in this country. We thank Prime Minister Carney, Minister Champagne, Minister Miller and the Government of Canada for recognizing that investing in Canadian music is an investment in who we are. This investment in the Canada Music Fund backs Canadian artists and the independent businesses that help bring their music to life. ”.

FACTOR, along with the Indigenous Music Office, CIMA, ADISQ, Bell Media, Spotify and more all participated in CRTC public hearings last year to discuss how to support Canadian Content.

Now, FACTOR welcomes the government’s investment and highlights how it will support the Canadian music sector.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “behind every dollar invested in canadian music are artists taking the next step in their careers and canadian companies helping them get there,” says symsyk. “Sustained investment makes it possible to look beyond the next release or tour and build for the future. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, several other music organizations across canada are celebrating the news, with the canadian live music association (clma) saying it is “thrilled to see government recognize the value that music brings to canada, its businesses, and its communities. ” The Canadian Independent Music Association (CIMA) calls the additional funding an “important step toward strengthening the industrial ecosystem that supports the development of great Canadian artists. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “for years, cima has argued that the best way to ensure canadians hear canadian voices is to build a strong ecosystem of dynamic, globally competitive canadian music companies serving excellent canadian artists,” says andrew cash, president and ceo of cima. This investment is an important commitment, and a clear indication that the government has listened to the music sector. “These are the businesses that discover, develop and nurture artists, produce and promote Canadian music, help build audiences and create opportunities for Canadian artists to reach listeners both at home and around the world. ”.

The federal government’s new investment intends to bring stability to the cultural sector as “longer-term policy, regulatory and market conditions evolve,” such as the Online Streaming Act, whose implementation continues to be the subject of much debate between the Canadian Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission (CRTC), streaming giants and the United States, which has made the CanCon fund requirements for major foreign-owned streaming services a sticking point in trade negotiations.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the live music sector is thriving more than ever in canada. In her role as chief commercial officer of Live Nation Canada, Melissa Bubb-Clarke is helping it soar towards new heights.

Berdasarkan laporan, on nov. 24, she will accept the Executive of the Year Award at Billboard Canada Women In Music, recognizing the important work she does behind the scenes, helping Canada’s live music giant scale its operations amid a rapidly growing industry, through collaborating and partnering with corporate brands.

The market leader in the country, Live Nation Canada has seen record success and revenue figures over the last few years, but in many ways Bubb-Clarke and the team she works with are just laying the foundation for an even bigger future.

Berdasarkan laporan, in its second season this summer, the 50,000-capacity rogers stadium welcomed a new record number of 20 concerts to toronto, drawing record-setting tours by headliners like bruno mars, bts, karol g and more. RBC Amphitheatre also kicked off its first season under its new name and partnership with RBC, which arrived alongside plans to become a year-round venue by 2030. There are more A-list artists coming to town than ever, but beyond welcoming shows, Bubb-Clarke is vying to create venues that offer an optimal experience for not just the artists playing them, but also the fans coming to see their favourite artist.

Preparing to accept the Billboard Canada Executive of the Year Award has given Bubb-Clarke the opportunity to reflect on the major strides she and her team have been making in the live music landscape over the past several years.

In an interview with Billboard Canada, Bubb-Clarke compares music to her work in sports at her previous company Maple Leafs Sports & Entertainment (MLSE), which owns the Toronto Maple Leafs and Toronto Raptors.

Berdasarkan laporan, “i can give you a million reasons why i think music is as much of a compelling offering, if not more, than sports. We do every demographic, every age group, all sorts of styles of music, I think we are super fan-friendly in that way. From a demographic standpoint, we’re serving everything to everybody with our 4,000+ shows that we do across Canada here with Live Nation. There are more concerts at Scotiabank Arena than there are [Maple] Leafs and Raptors games combined. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “i think we have been able to understand what the fans have come to get, what they have been able to experience at a sports venue. They want to be able to have nice food and go to a specific place post-show or pre-show and have a great overall experience. They’re looking for a similar experience at a show. ”.

In her dual role as the president of MusiCounts and the chief operating officer of CARAS, the organization behind the Juno Awards and the Canadian Music Hall of Fame, Kristy Fletcher influences every stage of a Canadian musician’s career.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, through music education charity musicounts, she’s there at the beginning, providing access to instruments and musical education to give youth a chance to make music in the first place. At CARAS, she’s able to foster and develop the industry and recognize artists at the Juno Awards. That continues all the way until the later stages of their career, when they become Hall of Famers.

Diungkapkan bahwa on nov. 24, Fletcher will accept the Impact Award at Billboard Canada Women In Music, recognizing the important work she does affecting musicians both onstage and in classrooms, from Rush’s surprise comeback performance at the 2026 Juno Awards to young students who might be Canada’s next breakthrough rock stars.

Sebagaimana diketahui, this year, musicounts announced a $1. 4 million donation to support music education in Canadian schools, the biggest investment in the company’s history. Through the MusiCounts School Music Funding Programs, 96 schools across the country will receive support for their music programs amid increasing budget cuts and deficits in Ontario and throughout Canada.

Diungkapkan bahwa “music is such a foundational and fundamental part of development and growth for kids,” fletcher says. We have seen so many studies [showing how] music supports strong and healthy mental health, and develops positive self-esteem. “Think of all of the incredible benefits that music has on kids. It’s a way to sort out their emotions or express their feelings and thoughts, and it can improve mental health among youth. There are studies showing improved cognitive abilities with playing music.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “musicounts has to be there to help fill in some of those gaps, and the gaps do grow. We’ve been doing this work for almost 30 years and we’ve allocated over $22 million to schools and community programs across the country. You would think we would maybe be nearing the end of the work we have to do, and that’s just not the case. But that has allowed us to increase our programming. We’re just scratching the surface. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, read the full interview here. — Richard Trapunski.

“Canada has influenced my music in many ways,” says Sean Paul.

The Jamaican star is the subject of the first episode of Billboard Canada News, live now.

Berdasarkan laporan, in a revealing half-hour interview hosted by alicia west, paul talks about the important role that canada played in his come-up. He guested on the Baby Blue Sound Crew song “Money Jane” with Toronto hip-hop and R&B heroes Kardinal Offishall and Jully Black.

Berdasarkan laporan, “i was just telling somebody last night. They asked me who was the first person to put you on, give you a collab? And I said Kardi. Kardi Offishall,” he says. “First person to pay me, first person to put me on a track, I always say. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, he also talks about shooting important breakthrough music videos “gimme the light” and “get busy” with canadian director director x (then little x) and dancer/choreographer tanisha scott, both longtime collaborators. His connection goes back even further, with his grandfather living in Scarborough, Ontario when he was young.

Diungkapkan bahwa it’s a wide-ranging conversation about his whole career, from his biggest chart hits to his collaborations with major pop stars like rihanna and sia. He also talks about his support of Jamaica following Hurricane Melissa.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, watch the full interview on billboard canada news below. — Richard Trapunski.

#467. Michael Mann Seeks to Reclaim Rights to Original ‘Heat’ Screenplay

📅 14 Nov 2026

Michael Mann Seeks to Reclaim Rights to Original ‘Heat’ Screenplay

Tanggal: 14 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://variety.com/2026/film/news/michael-mann-new-regency-heat-screenplay-lawsuit-1236947532/

Michael Mann, who is set to begin shooting the long-awaited “Heat 2” in January, is in a legal dispute with New Regency as he seeks to reclaim the copyright to his screenplay for the original film.

Berdasarkan laporan, new regency produced “heat,” released in 1995. The company filed a lawsuit on Friday arguing that it still owns the copyright to the original screenplay.

Diungkapkan bahwa earlier this year, mann’s lawyers sent termination notices invoking the right to reclaim the copyright. New Regency argues that the screenplay was a “work made for hire,” and is thus ineligible for copyright termination. Related Stories 'Off Campus' Sets Season 2 Release Date at Amazon Chris Pratt to Continue 'Terminal List' Story in 'Savage Son' Series for Amazon.

New Regency argues that Mann’s termination action clouds its ownership of the original “Heat,” and is seeking a declaration that the termination notices are void.

Mann’s lawyers intend to fight the lawsuit “vigorously,” his reps said in a statement.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “we will vigorously defend this action and are confident that the courts will vindicate michael mann’s statutory rights under the copyright act,” a spokesperson said. After 40 years Michael Mann is exercising the right of authors to reclaim their work and in this case Michael Mann’s original creation. “This filing has to do with original and personal writing Michael Mann did on multiple screenplays during the 1980s and which evolved into the iconic 1995 film ‘Heat’ that Mann wrote, produced and directed. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, mann developed the characters and the story that would become “heat” over two decades, beginning in the 1970s. According to the lawsuit, Warner Bros. acquired the rights to the “Heat” screenplay in 1994 in a deal with Mann’s loan-out company. The suit alleges that deal was explicitly a “work made for hire” agreement — not an assignment of rights — and that therefore it cannot be terminated.

Authors are allowed to terminate assignments of rights after 35 years under the Copyright Act.

Sebagaimana diketahui, according to the suit, mann’s lawyers initially told new regency that mann had assigned his rights to his loan-out companies in 1988, and was thus seeking to terminate that agreement. New Regency sought a copy of that agreement, and was told it was an oral agreement, the suit states.

Diungkapkan bahwa “the oral assignment on which the first termination notice is based supposedly derives from an oral agreement that mann allegedly made with himself, in which mann, like a shakespearean actor playing multiple parts, simultaneously spoke on his own individual behalf, as well as on behalf of mmco. and ZZY,” the lawsuit states.

Two subsequent termination notices were submitted cited other agreements, both of which New Regency claims are also invalid.

Berdasarkan laporan, warner bros. was originally set to produce “Heat 2,” but backed out of the project last year. Amazon MGM Studios has since acquired the film. Both Mann and New Regency have done deals with Amazon that account for the copyright dispute, with Mann assigning any rights he may reclaim to Amazon, according to the complaint.

In other words, however the dispute comes out, “Heat 2” should be unaffected.

“For clarification, this is unrelated to production of Heat 2 which will begin shooting on January 19,” Mann’s rep said in a statement.

#490. Prime Video's 2-Season Action Thriller Just Surged 307% To Become the No. 1 Streaming Original

📅 14 Nov 2026

Prime Video's 2-Season Action Thriller Just Surged 307% To Become the No. 1 Streaming Original

Tanggal: 14 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://collider.com/terminal-list-prime-video-action-thriller-streaming/

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, when it comes to the host of action thrillers that you can find on prime video, none have made quite the waves that the terminal list has. 1 on Streaming" territory just last week. Based on the popular James Reece novels by former Navy SEAL-turned-author Jack Carr, the two-season drama has soared in the streaming charts, with Variety reporting that the show had even jumped into "No. With over 1. 3 billion minutes watched, the David DiGilio-created thriller continues to exceed expectations and is a reminder that the conspiracy-minded military thriller is as strong as ever.

Sebagaimana diketahui, for fans who have followed the terminal list since the first season dropped back in 2022, this doesn't come as a surprise. It wasn't long before Jack Carr famously noted that the show was made for fans, and the budding action franchise has been better for it. Rather than cater to whatever was safe or perhaps politically correct, the Chris Pratt drama largely stuck to its guns and pressed forward by expanding on what made the show successful in the first place, business as usual. Although initial reviews for the book-to-screen adaptation were not in the show's favor, the audience scores were exceptional. That decision paid off, with the prequel, The Terminal List: Dark Wolf, and the second season, based on the novel True Believer, leaning more into the type of material fans were hoping for after that inaugural batch of episodes — even if there were some changes made to the source material. Over time, the show and its spin-off have become more well-received even by reviewers, and The Terminal List only continues to expand.

Diungkapkan bahwa of course, the terminal list isn't just a successful show on streaming; it's one of prime video's best. It's a harrowing but complex story that could only be told with the freedom that Prime Video offered DiGilio, Carr, Pratt, and the rest of the creative minds involved. Over the last several years, the Amazon platform has become known as the definitive home of the action thriller. Pratt's James Reece is a protagonist haunted by his loss, one who seeks to redeem himself for the actions he took against those who wronged him — including his best friend. Sure, it can be a bit gruesome at times, but that's the world of espionage and off-the-books military operations for you. Reacher and Jack Ryan alone would probably be enough to solidify this idea, but The Terminal List and its Dark Wolf prequel have proven over and again that there are differing flavors of the action/military thriller flavor that deserve our undivided attention. The good news is, they're not done yet.

Berdasarkan laporan, for those worried that the true believer adaptation may be the end of the story, never fear. In Collider's interview with showrunner David DiGilio, the creator explained that they are always thinking of ways to expand The Terminal List world beyond just James Reece and Ben Edwards (Taylor Kitsch). While no official confirmation has been made as to what those projects may be (or their current status), we do know that the next James Reece story will be a book-to-screen take on the third Carr-penned novel, Savage Son, one that "Reecer" fans are anxious to see brought to life. How this will look exactly — as either a third season or a standalone series building off previous installments — is currently a mystery, but the news that the folks in charge have plans for a quicker turnaround is exciting. Hopefully, that means we'll also be getting more of the Dark Wolf prequel soon as well.

Sebagaimana diketahui, although chris pratt may be best known for his big-screen roles in the mcu and jurassic world franchises (or his time on the sitcom parks and recreation), the terminal list has more than proven that the star has the chops to tackle more serious and thematic material with ease. And yes, that was before he was a well-known movie star. Sometimes things just work out, and in the case of The Terminal List, there's no doubt that Amazon made the right call in not only adapting these beloved military thrillers but also in finding its leading man. "[He] was the person I thought of playing the role as I was writing the book," Carr once explained on his YouTube channel when speaking about the events leading up to the Prime Video series. The next season can't come soon enough.

The Terminal List is available for streaming on Prime Video.

There, she managed to have two or three songwriting sessions a day with different colleagues, and her name reached the ears of Nir Seroussi of Interscope, who contacted her to learn more about her work. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, upon meeting seroussi, schell says he immediately made her feel “like family,” and after listening to a couple of her songs, introduced her to ben tischker of wide eyed entertainment — the very same “ben” she had originally been looking for — who is now her manager. “It was incredible!” Schell says. “Then Nir helped me place a couple of songs, including my first one, ‘PXTXS,’ for Fuerza Regida.

Sebagaimana diketahui, originally written as a bolero, “pxtxs” — part of fuerza’s album dolido pero no arrepentido — is a heartbreak song about trying to overcome a breakup through excess and self-destruction. It turned out very beautiful. “It was a song that got a lot of attention at the time because it was a bolero that wasn’t vulgar but very raw,” says Schell. “I remember they replicated what I was doing with my voice on a guitar, and then they made it more regional. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa through interscope, the hit “gabriela” by katseye also came about. ’ I didn’t even know KATSEYE was such a big group. He said, ‘This one,’ sent it, and that was it,” she recalls. “It was quite strange because it happened very fast. “Normally songs take much longer to come out, but two months later the song was released and I started receiving tons of messages: ‘Congrats, congrats. They needed me to write a bridge in Spanish, and I remember sending Nir two options. And well, obviously it came out, and with everything that happened with the song, I’m very grateful to be part of it. ”.

Since then, she mentions Rawayana’s “Bendito” (“It was super fun to write, a blast”) and Kany García’s “A La Niña Que Fui” (“It was very beautiful how we connected”) among her favorite collaborations.

Berdasarkan laporan, in her august cover story interview with billboard español, garcía praised schell as a “super-talented” songwriter while recounting how this song, now competing for a latin grammy, came to be. (Its songwriting credits also include Rafa Arcaute, Nate Campany and Richi López).

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “i called her to write. But when you sit with creative people who are seeing the picture from outside, they see things that you don’t. And I told myself: ‘How beautiful it is that sometimes, as a songwriter, I think I have to do it all myself, that everything has to come from my head. I had melodies in my head, but nothing concrete… And she said to me — because it wasn’t me, it was her: ‘Hey, how about writing a song to your inner child?'” García recalled. “It gave me chills, because she didn’t know that the project was heading in that direction. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa “just meeting her, and how i grasped what she wanted without her telling me,” says schell, “sometimes there’s this energy in the room that’s the most important, where the most magical songs come from, and i feel like we walked in and captured it right away. ”.

Although she has released some music as a singer in the past year — mostly collaborations with Sistek, Gonza Silva and LAGOS — Schell, currently signed to MPub and Wide Eyed Publishing, says her “calling” has always been “writing for others” and that she doesn’t plan to have a career as a performer.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “from the moment we met sara, we recognized an exceptional talent in her,” daniela méndez varón, head of a&r at mpub, tells billboard. “Her artistic sensitivity, versatility and vision as a songwriter set her apart, but it’s her human qualities that make her even more special. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa as for how she found out about her latin grammy nominations, the songwriter recalls going to bed exhausted after a long day’s work and not even setting her alarm to catch the announcement. “But obviously, I was nervous,” she says. ’ I was like: ‘Oh my God. “I left my phone’s sound on, and I got a call from producer Héctor Mazzarri, who’s one of my best friends — also nominated this year, by the way — telling me: ‘Congratulations. ’ And I’m like: ‘What happened?’ ‘Songwriter of the Year. '”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, meanwhile, her dad couldn’t be prouder: “he’s so happy. So he’s like: ‘I knew it from the beginning. ’ It’s very sweet. I mean, of course he could believe it. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, when asked who she’d like to write songs with, schell doesn’t hesitate. “Franco De Vita. You know, being from Venezuela, I grew up listening to him, and it was the music I listened to most with my grandparents,” she says with a smile.

#502. 5 Best New Movies And Shows To Stream This Weekend On Netflix, Prime Video, HBO Max, And More (Nov. 13-15)

5 Best New Movies And Shows To Stream This Weekend On Netflix, Prime Video, HBO Max, And More (Nov. 13-15)

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.slashfilm.com/2313651/best-movies-tv-shows-streaming-netflix-prime-video-hbo-max-november-13-15-weekend/

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, can you believe we're halfway through november? wild. 2026 is passing by alarmingly quickly, and we're about to hit full holiday mode as we approach Thanksgiving. but you don't need to get your turkey and stuffing recipes out of storage just yet. We've still got some time, and you should consider using that time to watch a whole bunch of stuff.

Diungkapkan bahwa yes, it's time to round up the buzziest, best, and biggest streaming releases for the weekend of friday, november 13 to sunday, november 15, which does include releases from earlier in the week as well. As always, the list is limited to releases new to major streamers entirely (case in point: though the hit Colleen Hoover movie adaptation "Reminders of Him" only just came to Netflix, it was already available on Peacock, so that's a nonstarter here), but between a killer dinosaur flick, a new thriller starring an Oscar winner, a drama with an innovative structure, a fresh literary adaptation, and the continuation of a massive fantasy series, you've got plenty of options.

Berdasarkan laporan, if you didn't get enough jessica chastain in this year's admittedly silly horror movie "other mommy," you're in luck — she has a new film coming to netflix this weekend. As Misty tries to locate Charlie, other family secrets come to light, and she tangles with a criminal underbelly in Nashville in the process. Written and directed by Shana Feste (the filmmaker behind "Country Strong," "Run Sweetheart Run," and "Boundaries," to name a few), "Heartland" stars the Oscar-winning Chastain as Misty Jones, a country singer who's retired from show business but has to come out of her self-imposed solitude to find her niece Charlie Heart (real country singer Carter Faith), who's gone missing. and the fact that Misty is notoriously prickly and was nicknamed the "queen of mean" in her days as a country star certainly doesn't help matters.

Diungkapkan bahwa "heartland" also stars john hawkes, garrett hedlund, jennifer nettles, and ross lynch in supporting roles, but chastain is the real draw here, and whether or not you saw or loved "other mommy," you should check this pick out. "Heartland" drops on Netflix on November 13, so stay in this Friday and have a movie night.

Sebagaimana diketahui, if you, like me, love dark and twisted thrillers, you're probably familiar with the name karin slaughter. Indeed, ABC's massively successful procedural "Will Trent" is adapted from Slaughter's novel series about an Atlanta detective (though it tones down some of the more depraved stuff found in the books), and in 2022, Netflix released a series adaptation of Slaughter's novel "Pieces of Her" starring Toni Collette and Bella Heathcote in its lead roles. (Incredibly, I'm pretty sure that's her actual name. ) Even casual TV fans are aware of her, even if they think they're not. Now, Slaughter's book "The Good Daughter" is getting an adaptation from Peacock, and it stars two of the most talented women acting today: Rose Byrne and Meghann Fahy.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the premise of "the good daughter" is enticing on its own: decades after a brutal and violent incident in the quinn family, sisters samantha and charlotte (byrne and fahy) still reside in their hometown of pikeville, georgia, with charlotte working in law enforcement. Byrne and Fahy are both excellent on the show, and they're joined by Brendan Gleeson, Harper Steele, and Paula Malcomson, just to name a few. Hence, when she starts looking into a particularly violent crime, Charlotte is struck by her own experiences, as is Samantha — and new family secrets come to light. So, whether or not you're already a fan of Slaughter's body of work, you'll definitely want to get acquainted with "The Good Daughter," which dropped all of its episodes on Peacock on Thursday, November 12.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, peter jackson's "lord of the rings" film trilogy was a cinematic triumph when it released over the course of three years in the early 2000s, and it stands the test of time (though, the same can't really be said of his interminably drawn-out three-part "hobbit" prequel). So, if you've already watched the extended versions of every single "Lord of the Rings" movie thousands of times, I've got great news: Amazon Prime Video has a "Lord of the Rings" TV show, and it's entering its third season.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "the lord of the rings: the rings of power," which has been running since 2022, takes its lore from the appendices of j. Tolkien's massive fantasy tomes (but notably not Tolkien's "The Silmarillion" due to rights issues, so that has yet to be fully adapted). There are some "familiar" faces here from the Jackson movie trilogy, like Galadriel (Morfydd Clark) and Elrond (Robert Aramayo), but "The Rings of Power" admirably expands the world of Tolkien during the second age of Middle-earth. This is also, incidentally, when the Rings of Power (that's the title) were forged, which led to the rise of the Dark Lord Sauron (Charlie Vickers). R. R. As such, there's plenty to explore as this series forges ahead.

Berdasarkan laporan, the first four episodes of "the lord of the rings: the rings of power" season 3 dropped on amazon prime video on november 11. Two more will arrive on November 18, and the season will wrap up one week later on November 25.

Berdasarkan laporan, i truly cannot believe a movie as delightfully weird and ambitious as "the end of oak street" got made in the first place, but i sure am happy that it did. (There's also a family dog, Starbuck, and don't worry — nothing bad happens to him. That's as close to a spoiler as I'll get. David Robert Mitchell ("It Follows," "Under the Silver Lake") helmed this ode to dinosaur movies, summer blockbusters, and 1980s Steven Spielberg classics, which stars Ewan McGregor as Greg Platt, Anne Hathaway as his wife and aspiring writer Denise, Maisy Stella as the couple's eldest child Audrey, and Christian Convery as their son and youngest Brian. ) The Platts are an everyday family with everyday problems — Greg is secretly working as a pizza delivery driver after losing his job, while Denise is growing dissatisfied with their suburban life — but one night, a storm hits and traps them all in a bizarre prehistoric playground full of dinosaurs. This sounds almost magical, but here's the thing: those dinosaurs are starving.

Diungkapkan bahwa on one level, "the end of oak street" is the only movie in existence, as far as i'm aware, where you can watch anne hathaway wreak havoc on dinosaurs with a shotgun. What "The End of Oak Street" is above all else, though, is fun. On another level, it's a treatise on the importance on family, and on another level, it's an audacious science-fiction story with a little bit of time travel and a lot left unexplained. and it's streaming on HBO Max as of November 13.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in the aughts, "24" innovated a new style of episodic television by using a real-time conceit as a spy tries to save the world. Decades later, "The Pitt" used that same structure to great effect for its real-time experience of working a busy 15-hour emergency room shift. Apple TV's new drama series "12 12 12," though, is even stranger. Created by creative partners Jim Keeble and Dudi Appleton, "12 12 12" stars Anthony Mackie and Jamie Dornan as Jack Strickland and Bobby Galvin, two men involved with a high-risk heist in Zürich.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, so, how does "12 12 12" tell its story? as former fbi agent strickland and master criminal galvin circle each other in europe, the heist in zürich is where they eventually meet. and Keeble and Appleton use three timelines within each episode. First, you get the 12 months of planning the heist, followed by the 12 hours required for said heist — and finally, the 12 days' worth of heist-related aftermath. "12 12 12" also stars Jack Kesy, Kali Reis, Ólafur Darri Ólafsson, and Patrick Fabian in supporting roles, and its first two episodes are streaming on Apple TV as of November 13.

Producer Kevin J. Walsh Had Seen It All. Then ‘Being Heumann’ Came Along

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-features/being-heumann-kevin-j-walsh-1236754923/

Diungkapkan bahwa the oscar-nominated producer helped open doors for the disabled community on the set of sian heder's latest pic: "i'm as proud of what we did behind the scenes to redefine access as i am of the quality of this movie. ".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, being heumann producer kevin j. Walsh is not easily rattled.

Berdasarkan laporan, after all, the boston-area native served in a variety of assistant roles for scott rudin, steven spielberg and tommy mottola before eventually spending more than five years running ridley scott’s company, scott free. There, he shepherded a dozen pictures, four of them directed by Scott, including All the Money in the World (2017), The Last Duel (2021), House of Gucci (2021) and Napoleon (2023). In other words, he’s as battle-tested as they come.

Berdasarkan laporan, yet the prospect of helping coda director sian heder tell the story of judith “judy” heumann’s herculean fight to make the world more accessible for disabled people made walsh’s blood run cold. Related Stories Movies Sam Levy, Jamie Ramsay Offer Advice to Up-and-Coming Cinematographers: "What You Guys Do Lives Forever" Movies Ridley Scott Will Miss Academy's Governors Awards, Accept Honorary Oscar Remotely (Exclusive).

Sebagaimana diketahui, “when sian first asked me, ‘why do you want to do this?’ my answer truly was, “because the movie fucking terrifies me,’” walsh tells the hollywood reporter in support of being heumann’s nov. 13 release on Apple TV.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in 1977, disabled rights activist judy heumann helped organize the landmark section 504 sit-in, a nationwide protest aimed at compelling hew secretary joseph califano to finally sign the long-delayed regulations implementing section 504 of the rehabilitation act of 1973. Heumann and her fellow disabled activists occupied federal buildings across the country for more than three weeks until Califano finally put pen to paper.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the regulations secured civil rights protections for disabled individuals and helped direct billions of dollars toward making federally funded infrastructure more accessible, including through curb cuts, wheelchair ramps, wider public restrooms and designated parking spaces. The movement also helped pave the way for the more sweeping Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990.

Berdasarkan laporan, walsh and heder knew that if they were going to dramatize heumann’s david-versus-goliath tale, the only way to honor the late disabled pioneer was to bring her story to the screen authentically. That meant casting more than a dozen key roles with disabled actors and practicing what the movie preaches by creating an accessible, equitable set that could accommodate the ensemble’s unique needs.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the rub was that no such blueprint existed, and there was only one wheelchair-accessible trailer in all of north america. Working alongside a ten-person accessibility team and a crew that included disabled artisans and technicians, Walsh, Heder and their partners customized the Being Heumann set, taking extra precautions for the cast and ensuring direct access to personal and hair/makeup trailers.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “we did experience a handful of califano-type people, just not from the studio side. It was more, You can’t do it this way. It’s never been done this way,” Walsh shares. Apple was great. “But we needed to ignore history and really try to recreate how people make movies. I’m as proud of what we did behind the scenes to redefine access as I am of the quality of this movie. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, michael patrick thornton, who plays a supporting role opposite ruth madeley’s lead turn as judy, put matters into perspective in a way walsh will never forget. As one of the most accomplished disabled screen and stage actors of the last 25 years, Thornton found that Being Heumann offered him a first-time experience that most actors likely take for granted.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “on his first day, he got into the hair and makeup trailer and started to cry. He said, ‘In my whole career, I’ve never, ever seen the inside of a hair and makeup trailer,’” Walsh recalls. “He went on to describe it to me personally and said, ‘You don’t understand. But I feel like I’m one of everyone here. Normally, I’m in a closet getting ready on my own. This is Shangri-La for an actor who’s disabled. ’”.

Below, in a conversation with THR, the Manchester by the Sea producer also discusses his company’s prolific output in the 2020s, plus his extensive upcoming film and TV slate.

Berdasarkan laporan, when we last spoke for napoleon three years ago, the actors’ strike had just ended, and there were a lot of questions as to what the new normal would be. What did the answer end up being for you and The Walsh Company?.

Diungkapkan bahwa we’ve been lucky. Echo Valley did have to shut down because of the writers’ strike, so we went back to finish it. We got to make three or four movies during the strikes, which was really something. We were able to keep shooting in Europe. Overall, we’ve now made five movies at Apple since [launching the Walsh Company and signing there in 2022]. We then got a little independent film made called Miss You, Love You, and we’ve since made four films at Apple. So COVID and the strikes impacted us, but we were largely able to keep going.

Is it harder to set things up now? Or is it about the same?.

Diungkapkan bahwa it’s been about the same for us. The head of a streamer once joked, “Everybody’s been drinking at the bar for free, and now they’ve got to pay their tab. We’ve been on a really good pace setting things up, but getting things made and securing that green light is always harder. ” So those days are gone when a streamer would green-light a $50 million to $70 million movie and say, “Hey, good luck. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i have to really work for the green light now, but these streamers and studios need product. So I’m lucky to be in that small percentage of people who are still getting movies produced. We’ve set up a bunch of movies, and we’ve made five since we last talked. We’ve also started a TV business.

Diungkapkan bahwa you and sian heder both have deals at apple. Did they play matchmaker between the two of you for Being Heumann?.

Diungkapkan bahwa i actually met sian during a party at ben affleck’s house. I had been looking for the right thing, but Apple ultimately did play matchmaker because we both had deals there. We both grew up outside of Boston, and we both expressed a desire to work together. They said they needed someone to come on alongside [producer] David Permut, who had identified the rights and done a great job developing the script. So Sian and I really bonded as we started to talk about the challenges of this movie, and I was excited to jump in with her.

Sebagaimana diketahui, you mentioned your fellow producer david permut. Do you know the story of how he fended off Jean-Marc Vallée to acquire the rights to Judy Heumann’s story?.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i don’t know the details surrounding the jean-marc of it all. I do know that David and Sian arrived at Judy separately, but then they quickly came together. I came in much later, but I was really happy to play a pivotal role in the development of the script and the execution of the movie.

Sebagaimana diketahui, judy was at a decision-making point when sian cold-emailed her [in 2020]. One of Sian’s best friends, who was an accessibility coordinator on Crip Camp, had told her to watch the documentary [co-starring Heumann]. m. ” Judy wrote back 20 minutes later and said, “I’m making the decision on who I’m going to make this movie with today. Sian asked, “Why should I watch it?” And her friend said, “This woman needs to have a movie made about her. So if you can get on the phone with me tonight at 5:00 p. , you’ll be in the running. ” So Sian watched Crip Camp, and she emailed Judy that same day to say, “Hey, I’m really interested in your story. ” Sian quickly finished her book and called her that night.

Sebagaimana diketahui, coda came out in august 2021. Sian’s follow-up is now out in November 2026. It won the Oscar for best picture in March 2022. Was she indecisive about how she wanted to spend her Oscar capital? Or did it just take a while to get Being Heumann across the finish line?.

Berdasarkan laporan, i think she’s just really exacting. She’s relentless in making sure something is really excellent, well done and well researched. So she took her time just to make sure it was the movie she wanted to commit to. People misuse the word picky when exacting is the better word. She had a lot of opportunities with other films and studios, but they weren’t quite the right fit for her or an exact match with her DNA.

Diungkapkan bahwa she really appreciates and supports underdogs — and this story certainly tells the ultimate underdog story. So it took time for her to get the script right, and then it took time for Apple to finally make that turn to say, “Okay, we’re going to make Being Heumann. ” That’s just part of the normal process of getting movies green-lit.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, i’m ashamed to admit i never fully realized how life-changing a curb cut could be for someone with a disability. And, as the movie points out, so many people were naive to that reality. But after watching Being Heumann, I’ve started noticing all the other forms of accessible infrastructure that Judy Heumann and her allies fought to establish.

Diungkapkan bahwa you’re right that people don’t realize it. People do not realize how vital and how prevalent curbs cuts and other forms of barrier-free access are. Judy fought for them at a time when they didn’t exist. This affects everyone. One of my favorite lines in the movie is about how anyone at any time can become a part of this subset of disabled people. We’ve done probably 15 Q&As over the last month, and you’d be surprised how many people are affected, whether it’s personally or through their siblings, their parents, their cousins, et cetera. And if we’re lucky enough, we’ll live a long time — long enough to use a cane or a walker or a wheelchair.

Diungkapkan bahwa hollywood, meanwhile, still has very few figurative curb cuts for the disabled community, whether it’s telling their stories or hiring their performers. Did you encounter your own Joseph Califano types in trying to get this movie made?.

Diungkapkan bahwa we did experience a handful of califano-type people, just not from the studio side. It was more, You can’t do it this way. Apple was great. But we needed to ignore history in a way and really try to recreate how people make movies. It’s never been done this way. I’m as proud of what we did behind the scenes to redefine access as I am of the quality of this movie.

Diungkapkan bahwa access is the word i keep coming back to for everything about this movie. We made sure that disabled people had access to every single thing that an able-bodied crew member had access to — and then some. We created a film set with access to trailers and ramps. That happened through a lot of hard work, ingenuity and research by our great team of people.

Did any wheelchair accessible Star Waggons exist?.

Berdasarkan laporan, there was one in all of north america. We actually ended up cutting the backs off some trailers and creating lifts to bring actors up into the hair and makeup trailer. We had a series of ramps built by our construction team and grips, which we laid out to lead actors to any trailers that weren’t accessible. It made such a difference.

Sebagaimana diketahui, one of our actors, michael patrick thornton, who plays ed roberts, the self-described “artichoke” in the movie, had been working for 30 years in the movie business. He’s a huge Broadway actor and a big TV actor. He just finished a Broadway run with Keanu Reeves in [Waiting for Godot].

Sebagaimana diketahui, on his first day, he got into the hair and makeup trailer and started to cry. He went on to describe it to me personally and said, “You don’t understand. But I feel like I’m one of everyone here. This is Shangri-La for an actor who’s disabled. They asked him what was wrong, and he said, “In my whole career, I’ve never, ever seen the inside of a hair and makeup trailer. ” I was so floored by that story and what we had done to achieve it. Normally, I’m down the hall in a closet getting ready on my own. ” So, as a seasoned disabled actor, he could see the difference.

Was there extra crew to accommodate the disabled cast?.

Sebagaimana diketahui, we had a 10-person accessibility team at all times. We provided masseuses, nutritionists and round-the-clock care. We had people transferring disabled actors from their regular wheelchairs to period wheelchairs. We’d give them time for stretches and breaks. We had a lot of disabled crew members working with us as well.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, but we made a lot of mistakes throughout the process. It’s one of the reasons why I did the movie. We had to refine it and hone it and get it better and better. ” I wanted to figure out all these issues. When Sian first asked me, “Why do you want to do this?” my answer truly was, “Because the movie fucking terrifies me. It was just really important for me to learn this new skillset. But with a good team around us, we were able to achieve it.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, there are so many great disabled actors in this movie who had never acted before. So, for them, it was like, This is how movies must work all the time. They’d never been in a film before, much less a soundstage or a set. (Laughs. ).

When it came to casting Judy and the other 504 protestors, how large was the talent pool of disabled actors?.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, you might be surprised to hear this, but there are a lot of really talented people. Our casting directors, Bernie Telsey and Adam Caldwell, really put the spotlight on that community. Had we not tried to authentically cast people with the actual disabilities of the characters they’re portraying, we wouldn’t have found that talent.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, for judy, it was a bit more specific. We had to find a disabled person who has the charisma and acting chops to lead a movie, but also possess the same kind of ferociousness and tenacity that Judy had. So there aren’t a lot of Ruth Madeleys out there.

Hopefully, this movie opens more doors for everyone.

Berdasarkan laporan, yeah, my hope is that people will shine a spotlight on these actors so that they’ll be considered for other parts. We’re developing a TV show right now for an A-list TV actress, and I’ve pitched one of our disabled actors, Andrew Pilkington, to play her sibling. So I just said, “How great would it be if he were the brother of this actress? That would provide a whole other layer of complexity to this show. He plays Hale Zukas in Being Heumann, and he communicates with the antenna on the board. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa i’m also doing the team hoyt movie at netflix with producers gotham chopra and tom brady, and [directors] nat faxon and jim rash. I’m bringing Andrew Pilkington on because he’s a producer in his own right, and he’s going to help me with authenticity. We have an actor who has cerebral palsy, and he’ll oversee the way we make the movie.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, so there is a lot of talent in front of the camera and behind it. It’s just a matter of redefining the norms of casting actors in movies and TV shows and learning to look at everyone all at once. Again, access.

One of the best performances of the year was given by a disabled actor named Steve Way on the series Furious, which was partially directed by Cory Finley, who you helped launch by way of Thoroughbreds.

Diungkapkan bahwa yes, steve is incredible. I just read in the trades a couple days ago that Ramy Youssef and Steve are doing a body swap comedy, which is really interesting. She chatted with him, but Steve had some conflicts regarding this movie. What Steve and Cory and [creator] Liz Meriwether did on that show is amazing. We’re actually getting ready to start prep on Cory’s next film. Sian knows Steve. It’s coming up next year with a really good cast.

Berdasarkan laporan, i admire how honestly being heumann portrays its disabled characters. In other words, the film doesn’t portray them as infallible saints simply because they’re disabled. They’re generally altruistic, but they still make mistakes and give in to their impulses, like we all do. Did the ensemble also appreciate this unvarnished take?.

Diungkapkan bahwa they totally did. One of the most amazing feats of the movie is that each person you meet has their own little 180-degree turn. Early, early on, before prep, I said, “There’s too many people to service, Sian. I’m glad you mentioned that because one of the geniuses of Sian Heder is that she’s able to create an arc for all 15 of these characters. And I will say she proved me wrong. I don’t know if you’re going to get around to all of it. ” And she did. And so the actors loved that.

Diungkapkan bahwa a lot of times, when we see disabled characters, they’re either perceived as saintly or bitter because they’re dealing with their disability, but they are like anybody else. They just happen to be in a wheelchair or unable to access certain things that non-disabled people have access to. So the actors really appreciated how layered and different all these characters were.

Diungkapkan bahwa i was also impressed by how they let their personal experiences shine through in their characters quite a bit. If you recall the testimonials in the movie, Sian wisely guided and directed them to look inward a bit as they were telling those stories about their disabilities. That infused the film with a certain credibility, but also emotion.

Mark Ruffalo and Dylan O’Brien both fit their roles so well, but the cynical viewpoint is that you needed a couple names to appease the powers that be.

Berdasarkan laporan, they just responded well to the material. Stick to this number, but go make the film. [Apple TV bosses] Zack Van Amburg, Jamie Erlicht, and Matt Dentler really got behind this movie and said, “Go make the film. Don’t get me wrong, it’s always beneficial to have movie stars help open a film and bring awareness to a film. ” So we didn’t need any real names. But Apple was supporting this film through and through, head to toe. We were just lucky to get Mark and Dylan.

Berdasarkan laporan, mark is a once-in-a-generation-level actor. He could be perceived as a cold, simple villain, but he’s really a guy who’s just trying to do his best. He is perfect in the role of Califano. I spoke to him this morning in fact. We’re working together on another project that he’s going to star in and direct. It’s a very complex, layered part. And at the end of the day, he tips his hat to Judy, nicely, by saying, “Well fought. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa dylan is another wonderful actor with a huge following, so we got lucky to have those guys help raise awareness of the film. But we didn’t really need them.

Diungkapkan bahwa the postscript says that the fight for disability rights is far from over. Do you happen to know what the outstanding issues are?.

Berdasarkan laporan, yeah, a lot of these section 504 rights and regulations are now being conflated with the argument about transgender rights. They all fall under the same umbrella. So, in 14 states right now, they’re trying to repeal funding for some of these Section 504 rights because of other rights that fall under that umbrella. There was a big article about this in Time magazine within the last couple of months.

Sebagaimana diketahui, what people don’t understand is that you’re talking about taking away curb cuts, elevators and access for disabled people in our community. If you’re against the idea of a person in a wheelchair being able to access a federal building, a post office or a place to get their passport renewed, you’re on the wrong side of history. This is why it’s super important, and it saddens me that we’re still having this conversation 50 years later. It’s just that simple. So you have to look closely at what you’re reading, what you’re voting for and who you’re supporting.

Diungkapkan bahwa i spoke to tom pelphrey and louis leterrier not too long ago, and your sci-fi action-thriller with them, liminal, came up. What else are you excited about on the Walsh Company slate?.

Berdasarkan laporan, i’m really excited about louis’ movie. Besides Tom, it has Vanessa Kirby, Yahya Abdul-Mateen II, Tracy Letts and Franka Potente. He’s got a murderer’s row of great actors. So we’re in post on that right now.

Diungkapkan bahwa we’ve also had a rocket-ship start to our tv business. We hired an executive named Danny Feldheim about a year and a half ago, and we’ve set up ten TV shows in that time. We have five or six shows at Apple, a show with John Mulaney and Langston Kerman at HBO and another great show called The Hawk with Dave Collard and Casey Affleck at Hulu. So we’re excited about being all over that side of the business.

Sebagaimana diketahui, we’re also prepping three or four movies for next year. We just got something in the last week that I’m most excited about. There’s a Black List script called Best Seller that was with Peter Rice until he left to take the [Netflix CCO] job. We got lucky enough to meet on it, and while it went out to 10 or 15 producers, we won that movie. So we’re really excited about putting it together and getting a director on it.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, we’re finally going to make adam and aaron nee’s next movie, calamity hustle, next year. We’re getting close on that deal with two actors.

Ryan Reynolds and Channing Tatum are no longer attached?.

Sebagaimana diketahui, it’s no longer ryan and channing. The Nee brothers have done a really good job on the script, and they’re ready to go. It’s going to be a couple other actors, but we’re really excited about it. They’ve said no to a lot of movies to make this movie.

You mentioned it earlier, but what’s the latest on Cory Finley’s next one?.

Sebagaimana diketahui, yeah, we’re going to make cory’s upcoming film [reasonable people] with paul rudd and sam rockwell, which will probably be a fall shoot. It’s a wonderful story about revenge in modern-day America. We’re out to another actor now, and we’re closing a deal with a really exciting financier who’s going to do it. It’s kind of like a present-day Hatfields & McCoys set in the suburbs. It has that same darkly comedic tone as Thoroughbreds, with really nuanced characters and a deep dive into the relationship between two fathers and one of the fathers’ brothers in this suburban community.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, then we have a really big film at apple that we’re getting quite close on for next year. It’s a Christmas movie. So it could be a busy year next year, but I’m honestly just lucky and happy to be making movies and doing what I love. Apple has been great to us, and I’m grateful they’ve given us a platform.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “obsession and backrooms” has been the most repeated phrase this year. Everyone’s been trying to discern what the takeaway should be. Rather than simply hiring more YouTubers or adapting unusual internet properties, is the real lesson to take chances on newer, original voices, regardless of platform or genre?.

Berdasarkan laporan, you’re right about original voices. Matisse Haddad, who wrote Best Seller, is an original voice. He has a Black List script called Drudge about Matt Drudge, which is also one of the best scripts I’ve ever read. There’s another great young writer named Cody Brotter who’s writing the Bon Jovi story for us at Universal. It’s one of her early screenplays, and it’s one of the best scripts I’ve read in a long time. We’re going to try to get that made.

Diungkapkan bahwa so it’s about finding young voices and just trusting youthful filmmakers. There’s a great script we love called The Toe by a writer named Mallory Westfall. It’s harder to make those kinds of movies. It’s completely bonkers and left of center and dark, but original and great and unlike anything you’ll read. Those [tonal seesaws], like Cory’s next movie, are harder lifts, but you’re fighting for originality at the end of the day.

Sebagaimana diketahui, there are filmmakers to be found on youtube, just like there’s filmmakers to be found everywhere. The directive at our company isn’t, Go find us an action movie or a romantic comedy. It’s just about keeping an open mind to originality and setting your own pace and not trying to copy something else. It’s always, What makes you sit up straight when you read it? Do you want to make it and why? That’s really all we look for.

Berdasarkan laporan, we’ve reached the dreaded ai question. But now there’s filmmakers like Doug Liman and Darren Aronofsky who are experimenting with it rather aggressively, while directors like Ben Affleck, Danny Boyle, and Ava DuVernay have acknowledged using it for minor details, such as animating old photographs. Initially, the creative community drew a hard line in the sand against its use. But as the scope keeps creeping outward, those minor details could soon become major ones, and entire departments could be gutted or downsized in no time. Maybe I’m being an alarmist, but do you think it’s inevitable at this rate?.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i don’t think you’re being alarmist, but i don’t think it’s inevitable, either. There’s always going to be human artistry that you need to harness.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, some people say, “graphic designers and previs artists and other visual artists are going to be gone. He did Boston Strangler with me. ” John P. Goldsmith, who was my production designer on Being Heumann, has a degree from Harvard — a master’s in architecture. On Being Heumann, he designed all the detailed lobby work, like the brass elevator buttons and the marbling, in the building the protestors storm. John took all of his education, his history, his experience, all of it, and made sure that it looks right. He’s a genius. All of that was constructed from scratch. People from Apple came to visit the set, and they couldn’t believe it.

Sebagaimana diketahui, it hearkens back to one of my first films in my early 20s when i worked as an assistant on the hours. So, Stephen Daldry, I believe, described the [dropped] shot to the production designer and the construction team. I walked through it, and I couldn’t believe how exact a match it was. We didn’t want to go back to the hotel location. It was flawless. The next morning, I came back to the stage at Pinewood, and the hallway of this hotel had been reconstructed. We dropped a shot while filming at a hotel in the south of London, and we moved back to the stage. We put the actors in the hallway, Julianne Moore, and we had the shot.

Sebagaimana diketahui, so, yes, there’s a way to use ai quite a bit in previs, in post and with vfx, but you still need to harness that type of human creativity. You need to have a team that executes at a high level. This is a community medium. You’re going to use AI as a tool. The filmmakers you mentioned — Danny, Ava and Ben — they’re using it as a tool in a great way. But if you ask any one of them, “Can you do away with human artistry and do your job?” they’d say that you can’t. I could not make Being Heumann without my producing team of Sian, David, Kevin Cleary and John Beach.

Berdasarkan laporan, we are using ai, for sure, with certain vfx stuff. There’s definitely some AI in the previs on bigger movies. But I came up working in a lot of different departments in moviemaking, and you will always need to harness artistic creativity. Without it, you’re going to have a movie that feels devoid of spirit. It’s going to look mechanical, and audiences are going to sniff it out.

Berdasarkan laporan, screenwriting, storytelling and directing need to keep redefining. Those areas can’t be iterative. If you’re going to be iterative with AI, you’ll just be rehashing old movies and old stories. So you need human creativity to explore other areas, and that’s where you’ll find your Backrooms and Being Heumanns, movies that have not been done before.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i’ve asked this question off and on over the years, but i play rocky has given me permission to dust it off. I love narrative features about the making of beloved movies. So out of all your projects, which one warrants the I Play Rocky treatment?.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, oh man, that’s such a hard question. It was an incredible movie. I actually attended an AMPAS lunch this past weekend, and coincidentally, I was seated next to Mark Ricker, my production designer, on that movie. I had such a good time on The Way, Way Back. We talked about how it was his favorite movie ever.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, everyone rented beach houses alongside each other. We would walk to work every day, shoot the movie and come home. That was a great moviemaking experience for the comedy of it, because [co-directors] Nat [Faxon] and Jim [Rash] and I would go to dinners and get cocktails with all our wonderful comedic actors each night. Toni Collette, Allison Janney, Steve Carell, Sam Rockwell, Maya Rudolph and the rest of our wonderful cast all lived on the beach together. So there’s definitely a behind-the-scenes element to that.

Berdasarkan laporan, but then there’s the scope and scale of the ridley movies and those experiences. Napoleon was jaw-dropping to film and create. Seeing the scope of it made me pinch myself quite a few times and think, How did I get here? How did I get here from making a tiny little independent film 28 years earlier?.

Would [script doctor] Paul Thomas Anderson be the second or third-act twist in the Napoleon making-of movie?.

Diungkapkan bahwa (laughs. The filmmaker was so taken with Walsh’s look that he cast him in The Master. [Writer’s Note: In the early 2010s, Walsh attended a wedding officiated by Anderson. ) Yes, the Paul part of that process was great and really rewarding to watch. I actually got to meet Paul much, much earlier than that. ].

Sebagaimana diketahui, then i would say house of gucci, just with the legendary cast and the postcard-like tour of italy. I got to watch Al Pacino, Jeremy Irons, Gaga, Adam Driver and Jared Leto. We made the movie in Rome, Milan, Lake Como and the Alps. It was a wonderful front-row seat to moviemaking with Ridley at the helm. He’s one of a kind.

***Being Heumann is now streaming on Apple TV.

Isla Fisher & Blake Ritson Join Al Pacino In John Paul Getty III Kidnapping Pic ‘Captivated’

Tanggal: 14 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://deadline.com/2026/11/al-pacino-captiviated-isla-fisher-blake-ritson-1237223529/

Sebagaimana diketahui, exclusive: isla fisher and the gilded age‘s blake ritson have boarded the al pacino thriller captivated inspired by the extraordinary true story of the 1973 kidnapping of john paul getty iii. Dito Montiel is directing with production underway in Calabria and Rome, Italy. Also joining the cast is Jackson Kelly (The Pitt, The Body). The feature project is set against the backdrop of 1970s Italy and is billed as a new interpretation and angle on the famed kidnapping story, previously unexplored in Ridley Scott’s All the Money in the World and the FX series Trust.

Berdasarkan laporan, captivated is produced by michael mammoliti and manasvi mamgai of 32red entertainment, alongside andrea bucko and nicky weinstock of sweetheart entertainment, and producer cassian elwes. Additional producers include Michael Jefferson, Poppy Shaw of Calcott Films, Vinod Bhanushali of Bhanushali Studios Limited (BSL) and Anamaria Jakic. Watch on Deadline Related Stories News International Insider: AFM Deep Dive; Walliams Scandal; 'Ebenezer' In London News Dark Sky Films Acquires 'ANSWR' Starring Moises Arias, Rain Spencer, Piper Perabo & Simon Rex -- AFM.

Diungkapkan bahwa producer and co-writer mammoliti says, “for me, this project is deeply personal. My family has a direct connection to these events, and I grew up with a very different understanding of the story than the one audiences have seen on screen. With Dito, our remarkable cast and our producing partners, we have an opportunity to bring a new dimension to a story the world thinks it already knows. ”.

“After a decade of work, we’re proud to finally share this film with audiences,” said Andrea Bucko, producer.

Berdasarkan laporan, “saro mammoliti’s story is utterly captivating, and i knew it needed a director who could capture its truth. Ritson is repped by Curtis Brown Group and Peikoff Mahan. EPs are Emanuele Moretti, Navneet Chugh, Jason Hope, Maria Breese, Tony D’Souza, Oliver Trevena, Nachiketa Bhatt, Alina Gorun, Dominik Madani, Kerem Ozmen, Philip Nesterenko, Elizaveta Chalenko, Frank Walker, Ali Zahar, Tomer Shmulevich, Alex Engemann, Ryan Hawkins, Nini Le Huynh, Jess Maestro, Gian Gabriele Foschini, Monica Ruffo, Hilary Goldstein, Filomena Cusano, Ada Bonvini of The Family, Jay Burnley, Manouj Gupta, and Dalton Piche of 7 Cult. CAA Media Finance and WME are handling domestic distribution. What made A Guide to Recognizing Your Saints so special was the raw grit Dito Montiel brings to his storytelling, and that’s exactly why we trusted him with this movie. Behind the camera is cinematographer Stefan Ciupek, whose credits include the Oscar-winning Slumdog Millionaire, Rumors and the SXSW feature Brother Verses Brother from Ari Gold. I’ve been a huge fan of his work for years, and he delivered beyond anything we hoped for. Co-executive producers are Jacob Martin, Thomas Eliopoulos II, Kayo Anderson, Yash Raaj Singh, Ravi Tilak, Izak Zebak, and Chelsea Tieu. Fisher is represented by Anonymous Content, Curtis Brown Group, UTA, and Sloane, Offer, Weber & Dern. Jackson Kelly is repped by Gersh and 11:11 Entertainment. ”Montiel’s previous directing credits include A Guide to Recognizing Your Saints and Fighting. Voltage Pictures is handling international sales on the film. Oscar winner Pacino is repped by CAA and Don Steele at HJTH.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, comments on deadline hollywood are monitored. So don't go off topic, don't impersonate anyone, and don't get your facts wrong.

Awards Circuit Podcast: The roundtable discusses the 'I Play Rocky' screenplay debate and the new Disney movie 'Hexed'.

For years, people have told me that Seth Rogen and I are voice twins.

Sebagaimana diketahui, sitting across from him at the middleburg film festival, deep in virginia horse country, even jeremy, the person recording our conversation, can confirm that the resemblance is very close. Even so, the year Rogen is having belongs entirely to him.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, coming off the historic emmy run of “the studio,” rogen could have gone anywhere next. He chose to travel into the world of darkly comic relationship drama “The Invite” and the 2D animated world of Alzheimer’s disease with “Tangles,” a one-two punch nobody could have seen coming. Berdasarkan laporan, in “the invite,” olivia wilde’s a24 dinner-party indie, rogen plays joe, a husband whose fraying marriage gets stress-tested over one excruciating evening with the upstairs neighbors, played by penélope cruz and edward norton. On paper, it sounds like a “another Seth Rogen” role. I think it’s his finest hour as an actor.
